title: J.K. Dobbins: Sean Payton is my favorite head coach I've ever played for
summary: "This organization is amazing," Dobbins said. "I was born to be a Bronco."
full_text: J.K. Dobbins signed a one-year contract with the Broncos last year, and this year, despite a strong offer from the Jaguars , he stayed in Denver on a two-year deal. Dobbins says Sean Payton is a big part of the reason he didn't want to leave. Dobbins, who rushed for 772 yards in 10 games before a season-ending foot injury last season, says there's no better coach than Payton. "When I first got here, I just felt the love," Dobbins said, via the team's website. " Sean Payton is my favorite head coach I've ever played for. It just all feels like family here. They believed in me from the beginning." The other head coaches Dobbins has played for in the NFL were John Harbaugh with the Ravens and Jim Harbaugh with the Chargers. At Ohio State he played for Urban Meyer and Ryan Day. For Dobbins, playing for Payton in Denver is as good as it gets. "This organization is amazing," Dobbins said. "I was born to be a Bronco. I know I was drafted to the Ravens and played for the Chargers for one year, but I think I'm truly a Bronco. All roads led to here. I said last year, I had to get over the mountain to get here, and I'm here. I'm here to stay." Payton said he expects a big season from Dobbins this year. "He was a big part of why we won 14 games last year, and sometimes that can get lost in the narrative," Payton said. "Certainly, he's been injured, and yet what we were able to do when he was healthy had a lot to do with where we ended up, so it was unfortunate. I believe in the player a lot." And the player believes in his coach.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Big Ten, SEC finally strike a deal on the Protect College Sports Act
summary: The so-called "Protect College Sports Act" had stalled, thanks in large part to lingering objections from the Big Ten and the SEC.
full_text: The so-called "Protect College Sports Act" had stalled, thanks in large part to lingering objections from the Big Ten and the SEC. On Friday, it all changed. Via Ross Dellenger of Yahoo Sports, the Big Ten and SEC reached an agreement with lawmakers regarding the bill that would ostensibly restore some order to the chaos flowing from decades of rampant antitrust violations. While also picking the pockets of those who play the most profitable sports. President Trump got directly involved in the effort to smooth out the lingering issues. Senator Eric Schmitt (R-Mo.) told Dellenger that a vote of the full Senate is expected next week. With a one-month recess looming, the Senate was running out of time to get something done before the midterm elections in November. The bill, if passed by the Senate, would still need to be passed by the House of Representatives. If passed, it would give the NCAA and the various conferences a limited antitrust exemption, allowing the one-time transfer rule to be implemented and create a stricter revenue-sharing cap. It would also prevent coaches from leaving their teams before a season ends — a/k/a "the Lane Kiffin Rule." The sticking points related to preventing schools from circumventing the limits on spending. Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas), one of the bill's sponsors, called it a "hard cap." Which will be a hard pill for the players to swallow. Their earning potential is about to be restricted, without collective bargaining or any real representation in the legislative process. But that wrinkle has been lost in the rhetoric aimed at making Americans think that, without Congressional intervention, sports swimming in cash (like football and basketball) would be in danger of collapsing. Then there's the reality that the restrictions on player pay in the high-revenue sports will help subsidize the low-revenue sports. With all the current talk of socialism and communism, the concept of capitalism is about to go out the window when it comes to the folks who have the skills to play the college sports that make the most money.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jimmy Haslam: Myles Garrett trade was Andrew Berry's decision
summary: Nearly two months to the day after the Browns surprised everyone by trading defensive end Myles Garrett to the Rams, Btowns owner Jimmy Haslam addressed the move in a Friday press conference.
full_text: Nearly two months to the day after the Browns surprised everyone by trading defensive end Myles Garrett to the Rams, Btowns owner Jimmy Haslam addressed the move in a Friday press conference. “That was Andrew’s decision," Haslam told reporters, referring to G.M. Andrew Berry. "I don’t know what Andrew shared with you yesterday or in the past, that’s something that — the conversations we’ve had for about a while before it was announced, and the Rams were a good partner there and kept it quiet. But, a decision like that, ownership is going to be involved, but it’s Andrew’s decision, Andrew’s recommendation — in this case, ownership left it there." Haslam was asked why he accepted Berry's recommendation. "Well, one, I think we got a really good player back, and I think you saw him today — a really good player who’s 25 years old and still on his rookie contract, so that’s the biggest reason," Haslam said. "And then we picked up a one, a two and a three, and I think we all realize the three years we didn’t have number one picks due to the Deshaun [Watson] trade — one of those years I don’t think we even had a second — and the value of those picks, as we’ve proved the last two years, are tremendous. Myles [Garrett] is an unbelievable player. I was thinking the other night — Jim Brown, Joe Thomas, Myles Garrett — they’re all first-ballot Hall of Famers, world-class people, and so it was not an easy decision, but we’ve made it, we’re moving on and excited about Jared [Verse] and excited about those three draft picks.” It was a surprising change of position by Haslam and the Browns after the 2025 season, one in which Garrett set the single-season sack record and was named the NFL's defensive player of the year. But, really, what did it do for the Browns? They won five games. Adding draft picks is a plus, given the draft picks that were squandered in the Watson trade. Those picks become cheap, young players who can (if drafted and developed properly) become key, long-term contributors. It was still a stunning shift by the organization. In 2025, Haslam said the team never gave the possibility of trading Garrett a " serious thought ," even though he demanded a trade publicly in early February and wanted to meet with Haslam in early March. (Haslam declined to do so .) A year later, the Browns did much more than give it a serious thought. They arguably could have gotten even more for him in 2025, without having to sign him to a new, market-setting deal that made Garrett decide to stick around.
author: Mike Florio

title: Maxx Crosby hears Cowboys' trade chatter: It doesn't change anything for me
summary: The Cowboys had interest in a trade for Raiders pass rusher Maxx Crosby.
full_text: The Cowboys had interest in a trade for Raiders pass rusher Maxx Crosby. They might still have interest. Dallas attempted to acquire the five-time Pro Bowler in March. The Raiders instead sent him to the Ravens for two first-round picks before reneging on the deal because of long-term concerns about Crosby's surgically repaired left knee. Cowboys owner Jerry Jones was asked earlier this week about walking away from a deal for Crosby and took offense to the question. “ We didn’t ,” Jones said, via Jon Machota of TheAthletic.com. “We did not walk away. That’s about all there is to say. We understood his injury well. We thought he could help us then. We were surprised by the way that was resolved. To interject anything about what we’re thinking or doing, because he went back to the Raiders, would be a mistake. He’s a Raider. “If the team is coming along well, then those things stay alive. If all of a sudden you don’t think it’s coming along, then those things don’t stay alive. It’s a good indicator of how good we feel about this team. . . . He’s such a Raider. He’s completely a Raider. He’s happy to be a Raider. Everything in the book. We shouldn’t even be having this kind of discussion.” The Cowboys' team doctor, Dr. Dan Cooper, was one of the doctors the Ravens consulted about Crosby. But Jones' comments Tuesday reignited speculation about a possible trade of Crosby to the Cowboys. Crosby heard the trade talk and brushed it off. "It doesn’t change anything for me, to be honest," Crosby said Thursday, via Jarrett Bell of USA Today. "People act like they don't. . . . If you're an athlete in this position, you see everything. Regardless, if you want to or not."
author: Charean Williams

title: Judge grants class-wide injunction in fifth-year lawsuit against NCAA
summary: The NCAA's adoption of a rule giving athletes five seasons of eligibility in four years has had a consequence that may have been unintended.
full_text: The NCAA's adoption of a rule giving athletes five seasons of eligibility in four years has had a consequence that may have been unintended. It shouldn't have been unforeseen. Via Daniel Hager of On3.com, a federal judge in Colorado has granted a class-wide preliminary injunction requiring the NCAA to declare eligible all athletes from the high school class of 2022 for a fifth season of competition. As it relates to the NFL, the ruling could open the door for any undrafted, and unsigned, free agents who graduated high school in 2022 to return to play college football in 2026. The ruling secures the ability of former Texas offensive lineman Cole Hutson, who recently secured a temporary restraining order pending an August 3 hearing, to play college football in 2026 — despite participating in Browns and Cowboys rookie minicamps on a tryout basis. The ruling does not give quarterback Diego Pavia an automatic path back to the NCAA , given that he was in the high school class of 2020. (He played junior-college football for two seasons.) That doesn't keep him from trying to get a court order of his own, if he wants to try to play a fifth season of NCAA football.
author: Mike Florio

title: UNC G.M. Michael Lombardi "welcomes the opportunity to clear his name"
summary: North Carolina isn't saying much about UNC football G.M.
full_text: North Carolina isn't saying much about UNC football G.M. Michael Lombardi, who has been placed on paid administrative leave. Lombardi had something to say on Friday night, via his attorney. “Michael hasn’t been told anything about the nature of UNC’s investigation and welcomes the opportunity to clear his name, which has already been sullied by baseless statements and innuendo on social media," lawyer Tom Mars said, via Pete Thamel of ESPN. "He is fully cooperating with UNC and expects the investigation will be swift, thorough, and fair. Michael would ask that people have the decency to let the process run its course before jumping to any conclusions about the nature of the investigation or whether there’s any merit to whatever has been alleged." North Carolina has said that it is investigating " allegations " regarding Lombardi. Thamel reported on Monday that the situation “stems from a human resources complaint filed by a former UNC front office employee .” It's not unusual for the subject of an investigation to know nothing in the early stages. In many cases, the employer speaks to the person against whom accusations are made as the last step, after all other relevant information is gathered. When UNC interviews Lombardi, he'll get an idea pretty quickly as to what it's about. For now, he's still getting paid. He's just not working. Whether he returns depends on the outcome of the investigation.
author: Mike Florio

title: Sean McVay on Aaron Donald: If there’s an arrow, it’s trending upward
summary: The Rams coach doesn't expect the defensive lineman to decide whether he returns until after the team's training camp ends.
full_text: At every media availability, Sean McVay is asked about Aaron Donald. It seems inevitable that the three-time Defensive Player of the Year will return to the Rams. McVay said he doesn't expect the defensive lineman to decide until the Rams return to their team facility in Woodland Hills. They are conducting training camp 25 miles south at Loyola Marymount University, with camp wrapping up Aug. 7. But McVay offered a positive update on Donald's future. "If there’s an arrow, it’s trending upward," McVay said, via Nate Atkins of TheAthletic.com. Donald, 35, has not played since 2023, his 10th season in the NFL. But he has stayed in shape, and the team's acquisition of two-time Defensive Player of the Year piqued Donald's interest in a return. The Rams open the season in Australia against the 49ers on Sept. 10.
author: Charean Williams

title: Inside the Chris Olave deal
summary: One of the various training-camp hold-ins ended on Thursday, when the Saints signed receiver Chris Olave to a new deal.
full_text: One of the various training-camp hold-ins ended on Thursday, when the Saints signed receiver Chris Olave to a new deal. Due to make $15.493 million in 2026, Olave added a four-year extension, reportedly worth up to $132 million. The full details of the deal have now made their way to PFT HQ. Here they are, per a source with knowledge of the terms: 1. Signing bonus: $35 million. 2. 2026 base salary: $1.293 million, fully guaranteed. 3. 2026 per-game roster bonus: $1.36 million total ($80,000 per game); fully guaranteed (but must be earned). 4. 2027 base salary: $13.64 million, fully guaranteed. 5. 2027 per-game roster bonus: $1.36 million total ($80,000 per game); fully guaranteed (but must be earned). 6. 2028 base salary: $23 million, guaranteed for injury at signing and fully guaranteed in March 2028. 7. 2028 per-game roster bonus: $1.36 million total ($80,000 per game); guaranteed for injury at signing and fully guaranteed in March 2028 (but must be earned). 8. 2029 base salary: $27 million, $13 million of which is guaranteed for injury and becomes fully guaranteed in March 2029. 9. 2029 per-game roster bonus: $1.36 million total ($80,000 per game). 10. 2030 offseason roster bonus: $3 million. 11. 2030 base salary: $29.76 million. 12. 2030 per-game roster bonus: $1.36 million total ($80,000 per game). The contract also includes $2 million in escalators for 2027 through 2030, based on performance in the prior season. The formula goes like this: $400,000 for being named a first-team All-Pro; $400,000 for making it to the Pro Bowl; $400,000 for 1,200 or more receiving yards; $400,000 for 101 or more catches; and $400,000 for 10 or more receiving touchdowns. (In four NFL seasons, Olave has hit none of those triggers.) The actual base value is $124 million, with a maximum value of $132 million. The new-money APY is $31 million, and the base value from signing is $27.898 million. The $1.36 million in per-game roster bonuses for each of the next five years gives the Saints protection against injury. In 2024, Olave missed nine games, mainly due to multiple concussions. He started 16 games in 2025. Of the amount, $52.653 million is fully guaranteed at signing. By 2027, $77.013 million is fully guaranteed. By 2028, $90 million is fully guaranteed.
author: Mike Florio

title: Malik Nabers doesn't practice Friday, John Harbaugh calls it "part of the process"
summary: The first days of Giants training camp featured a lot of positive reports about how wide receiver Malik Nabers has healed from last season's torn ACL, but there were none to add to the list on Friday.
full_text: '' The first days of Giants training camp featured a lot of positive reports about how wide receiver Malik Nabers has healed from last season's torn ACL, but there were none to add to the list on Friday. Nabers did not practice with the rest of the team on the third day of camp, but head coach John Harbaugh said that the day off was part of the effort to get Nabers ready for the start of the regular season after such a long layoff. "I think it’s part of the process ," Harbaugh said, via Mike Garafolo of NFL Media. "These guys will work through it. Every single day, it’ll be what it is that given day. He’s worked real hard, he’s made a lot of progress and that’s what we decided to do today." Nabers declined to put a target date on a full return when he was asked about playing in Week 1 this week, but that's obviously the goal and the wideout's practice schedule will continue to be managed with that in mind.
author: Josh Alper

title: Justin Jefferson trying to build connection with both quarterbacks
summary: Kyler Murray and J.J.
full_text: Kyler Murray and J.J. McCarthy are competing for the starting quarterback job in Minnesota. Justin Jefferson doesn't have a favorite for the job, wanting only for the best man to win it. “Right now, we don’t know who’s the number one,” Jefferson said, via Will Ragatz of Bring Me The Sports. “It’s all about having communication and connection with both of the guys until further notice. Coming out here and getting work with both of them, talking to both of them, making sure we all understand and [are] on the same page. “It’s a competition. It’s all on who comes to practice and who’s the better guy. At this point, it’s still early in training camp for any of us to understand or know who’s the number one guy. It’s all about pouring into both of them and making sure that, whoever’s the guy at the end of the day, we’re not starting over or starting fresh.” Jefferson is doing all he can to build a connection with both quarterbacks. If he has a favorite, he isn't saying. “I love a competition,” Jefferson said. “I always love a competition. I feel like a competition brings out the true dog in you, that true player within you. It’s all about who’s coming every single day with that fresh mentality, that every single day is a new day. Not dwelling on a past day, if it’s a great day or not. Moving on and stacking those days and being consistent.” Murray, who turns 29 in August, gets a second chance after going 38-48-1 in seven seasons in Arizona, with 20,460 yards, 121 touchdowns and 60 interceptions. McCarthy, 23, has made only 10 starts in two seasons since the Vikings made him a first-round pick, and he threw 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions last season.
author: Charean Williams

title: Stephen Jones says Cowboys investigating trades, big-name veteran signings
summary: The Cowboys have been trade-happy the past year in rebuilding their defense.
full_text: The Cowboys have been trade-happy the past year in rebuilding their defense. They traded Micah Parsons to the Packers in return for Kenny Clark and other compensation; they traded with the Jets for Quinnen Williams; and they traded with the Packers for Rashan Gary. They are trying to do even more before the start of the season. During his training camp kickoff news conference, owner Jerry Jones teased a trade discussion he had with another team's owner earlier this week. Executive vice president Stephen Jones continued the trade talk on Friday during an appearance on 105.3 The Fan. "We've got several things that we’re considering right now. Some of it trades; some of it signing guys," Stephen Jones said on the radio, via Tommy Yarrish of the team website. "A lot of these older players who have still got some tread on the tires can come in here and help you. It may come in the form of a trade; it may come in the form of a veteran signing as you move into camp." The Cowboys still need help at pass rusher and at inside linebacker. Veteran linebacker Bobby Wagner remains a free agent, but former Cowboys scout Bryan Broaddus, who is now on 105.3, told listeners to "keep an eye on Jordyn Brooks." Dallas had interest in a trade for Brooks this offseason, but the Dolphins wanted too much in return. Miami since has signed Brooks to a three-year, $51.3 million deal. The Cowboys also tried to trade for Raiders edge rusher Maxx Crosby this offseason. Jerry Jones said earlier this week that his team never stopped pursuing Crosby even after Baltimore reneged on its deal with the Raiders for Crosby. The Cowboys certainly seem intent on getting even more help on defense before the start of the season. Stephen Jones said Friday that the team is "far from done" acquiring players. "I'd be surprised if the starting players on this defense don't change over time," Jones said. "We're always looking to be better. We'll continue to monitor this."
author: Charean Williams

title: Giants OLB Adbul Carter's goal is Defensive Player of the Year
summary: As a rookie, Giants outside linebacker Abdul Carter earned two benchings, totaled four sacks and finished fifth in Defensive Rookie of the Year voting.
full_text: '' As a rookie, Giants outside linebacker Abdul Carter earned two benchings, totaled four sacks and finished fifth in Defensive Rookie of the Year voting. He has a much bigger goal for his second season. “ I want to be Defensive Player of the Year ,” Carter said, via Darryl Slater of nj.com. Carter "absolutely" thinks it is realistic and laid out the reasons. “Just my process and knowing who I can be — and a belief in myself,“ Carter said. ”I know what I’m capable of. I can be whoever I want to be." Carter had moments when he showed why he was the third overall pick, but he also proved unreliable with his habitual tardiness. “Everything happened the way it was supposed to," Carter said. "I learned from it, moved on from it. So I’m ready to go.”
author: Charean Williams

title: Panthers put rookie wide receiver Chris Brazzell on IR, sign tight end Chamon Metayer
summary: Panthers rookie wide receiver Chris Brazzell's season is officially over.
full_text: Panthers rookie wide receiver Chris Brazzell's season is officially over. The Panthers announced that Brazzell has been placed on injured reserve as a result of the knee injury he suffered at practice on Wednesday. Brazzell will have surgery to repair his lateral collateral ligament. A third-round pick from Tennessee, Brazzell was a first-team All-SEC selection last year who was expected to make an impact as a rookie, but now he'll spend the year rehabbing to prepare for the 2027 season. With their open roster spot, the Panthers signed tight end Chamon Metayer, who originally signed with the Steelers as an undrafted rookie in April but was cut by Pittsburgh in June.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Mike Evans: Deebo Samuel is a hell of a pickup for us
summary: Count Mike Evans among those happy to see Deebo Samuel is back with the 49ers.
full_text: '' Count Mike Evans among those happy to see Deebo Samuel is back with the 49ers. Evans, who joined San Francisco in free agency back in March, told reporters on Friday that he’s expecting plenty from Samuel, as he returns to the place where he’s spent most of his career. “ I love the way he plays the game ," Evans said, via David Bonilla of 49erswebzone.com. "I think he's going to bring what he brought before to the team — that energy, that versatility. Hell of a pickup for us.” Samuel spent his first six seasons with San Francisco before the club traded him to the Commanders last year. In 16 games for Washington in 2025, he recorded 72 catches for 727 yards with five touchdowns while taking 17 carries for 75 yards with a TD. Back in 2024 for the 49ers, Samuel caught 51 passes for 670 yards with three touchdowns while taking 42 carries for 136 yards with a TD.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Packers sign LS Cal Adomitis, cut K Lenny Krieg, WR Brenden Rice
summary: The Packers signed long snapper Cal Adomitis and wide receiver Kaden Prather on Friday, the team announced.
full_text: '' The Packers signed long snapper Cal Adomitis and wide receiver Kaden Prather on Friday, the team announced. Prather's agreement was previously reported. In corresponding moves, the Packers released kicker Lenny Krieg and waived/injured wide receiver Brenden Rice. Adomitis is a fifth-year player from the University of Pittsburgh who originally signed as an undrafted free agent with the Bengals in 2022. He played 49 regular-season games and three postseason contests in three seasons in Cincinnati. He was released toward the end of training camp last season. Adomitis ended up playing nine games for the Eagles last season before finishing the season on the Steelers' practice squad. Prather entered the NFL as a seventh-round pick of the Bills in 2025 but was waived/injured at the end of training camp. He helped the Louisville Kings win the UFL championship this spring. Krieg was signed earlier this week to compete with sixth-round pick Trey Smack for the kicking job. Rice, who was claimed off waivers from the Raiders in May, was on the non-football injury list. The son of Hall of Famer Jerry Rice joined Las Vegas’ practice squad late last season after also spending time on the practice squads of the Seahawks and Patriots. He was with the Chargers in training camp last summer.
author: Charean Williams

title: Tucker Kraft has no hesitation about practicing without a contract extension
summary: The Packers took tight end Tucker Kraft off the PUP list on Friday and he will start being phased into the team's practices over the near future.
full_text: The Packers took tight end Tucker Kraft off the PUP list on Friday and he will start being phased into the team's practices over the near future. Kraft has been rehabbing a torn ACL and said on Friday that doctors told him his knee looks "spectacular," which leaves him feeling like there's no reason not to dive into the practice work needed to get him ready for Week 1. Kraft's plans for ramping up his work do not include holding anything back while waiting for a contract extension to get hammered out with the team. “Absolutely. I understand other peoples' worries in that facet ," Kraft said, via Ryan Wood of PackersNews.com. "However, I myself, I'm just worried about getting back to who I was pre-injury.” If Kraft weren't coming off an injury, he might opt for a different approach to this summer's practices but getting back from an ACL requires him to go full speed ahead right out of the gate.
author: Josh Alper

title: Cam Skattebo: I do dumb things sometimes, but I learn from it
summary: Skattebo's botched backflip led to a meeting with John Harbaugh.
full_text: '' Giants running back Cam Skattebo's flubbed attempt at a backflip earlier this month earned him a meeting with head coach John Harbaugh. Harbaugh said this week that the message to Skattebo was that he needs to take care of himself and do what he can to be healthy. Skattebo, who missed the second half of his rookie season with a dislocated ankle, said on Friday that the message was received loud and clear. “Obviously I do some dumb things here or there, but I learn from it," Skattebo said, via Jordan Raanan of ESPN.com. "My coach talked to me and told me how he felt. I learned from it. Will I go do that backflip again? Probably not. We live and we learn and we move on.” Skattebo has deployed the backflip to celebrate touchdowns in the past and he didn't rule out doing them in that setting in the future. As long as points are going on the board and Skattebo has a cleaner finish, the Giants are likely to have a little less of an issue with the gymnastics.
author: Josh Alper

title: Cardinals sign CB Quinton Newsome
summary: The Cardinals signed cornerback Quinton Newsome, the team announced Friday.
full_text: ' The Cardinals signed cornerback Quinton Newsome, the team announced Friday. In a corresponding move, the Cardinals placed cornerback Jaden Davis on injured reserve with an undisclosed injury. Newsome most recently played with the Houston Gamblers of the UFL this spring. He appeared in 10 games, totaling 43 tackles, two tackles for loss, half a sack, four passes defensed, one forced fumble and a fumble recovery. He entered the NFL in 2024 with Denver as an undrafted rookie free agent from Nebraska and spent parts of the past two seasons on the Broncos' practice squad. While in college, Newsome appeared in 53 games and recorded 149 tackles, seven tackles for loss, three sacks, 18 passes defensed, an interception, two forced fumbles and two fumble recoveries.
author: Charean Williams

title: 49ers activate DT Alfred Collins from active/PUP
summary: The 49ers activated defensive tackle Alfred Collins from the active/physically unable to perform list, the team announced.
full_text: ''' The 49ers activated defensive tackle Alfred Collins from the active/physically unable to perform list, the team announced. Collins passed his physical and practiced on Friday after recovering from offseason shoulder surgery. He enters his second NFL season after being selected out of Texas in the second round of the 2025 draft. As a rookie, he appeared in 16 games with one start. Collins totaled 17 tackles, one tackle for loss, one sack, two passes defensed, two forced fumbles and a fumble recovery as a rookie. Running back Isaac Guerendo (pectoral), tight end George Kittle (Achilles) and defensive end Mykel Williams (ACL) remain on PUP.
author: Charean Williams

title: Chris Foerster on 49ers practice scuffles: Things happen on first day in pads
summary: The 49ers put on the pads for the first time this year during Friday's practice and things didn't take long to heat up on the field.
full_text: '' The 49ers put on the pads for the first time this year during Friday's practice and things didn't take long to heat up on the field. Reporters at the practice noted that running back Christian McCaffrey and linebacker Dre Greenlaw engaged in some post-play shoving after Greenlaw knocked his teammate to the ground after a catch. Linebacker Fred Warner and tight end Jake Tonges then got into it after another play, which led to the involvement of a few other players before things got broken up. Offensive line coach/assistant head coach Chris Foerster, who is acting as head coach while Kyle Shanahan recovers from his car accident injuries, said after practice that fights are a "waste of time and energy" but that he thinks Friday's scuffles were just an outgrowth of being in pads for the first time. "Your first day of pads ," Foerster said. "Everybody’s trying to set the tempo, set the tone. Things happen. Obviously you don’t want it to happen every day, but I don’t think it’s any more than a Day 1 issue." Given the injury histories of some of the players involved on Friday, Foerster is unlikely to be the only member of the organization hoping that things are calmer from here on out.
author: Josh Alper

title: OL Andrus Peat announces his retirement
summary: Veteran offensive lineman Andrus Peat announced his retirement on Friday.
full_text: Veteran offensive lineman Andrus Peat announced his retirement on Friday. Peat made the announcement in an Instagram post that said he " gave it everything I had " over the course of an 11-year NFL career. Peat was a 2015 first-round pick in New Orleans and he spent nine seasons with the team. He played for the Raiders in 2024 and appeared in six games for the Steelers last season. During his time with the Saints, Peat started 102 of the 111 regular season games he played. Peat was a Pro Bowl selection at guard from 2018-2020 and he also started six playoff games while with the team.
author: Josh Alper

title: What happens with the Bucs and Baker Mayfield in 2027?
summary: If, as it appears, quarterback Baker Mayfield doesn't sign a new contract with the Buccaneers until after the 2026 season, what happens next?
full_text: If, as it appears, quarterback Baker Mayfield doesn't sign a new contract with the Buccaneers until after the 2026 season, what happens next? The team will have, in theory, exclusive negotiating rights with Mayfield until the opening of the negotiating window in March. By then, Mayfield may be determined to see what the market will be for him in 2027. (There's a chance his agents already have an inkling as to the possible options.) The franchise tag will be available. With a cap number in 2026 of $39.975 million, the 2027 tag would be $47.7 million. As noted by the folks at Spotrac, Mayfield's current deal has a $30.15 million dead-money charge for 2027. Using the tag would result in Mayfield counting for $77.85 million against the cap in 2027. They could tag him and trade him, but they'd need to carry the extra $47.7 million in cap space until they do. Or the Bucs could let him walk away. The market would then determine his value. That's where it gets interesting. Via ESPN, Mayfield's camp pointed to quarterbacks whose contracts are currently north of $50 million in APY: Jordan Love ($55 million), Trevor Lawrence ($55 million), and Brock Purdy ($53 million). Right or wrong, deals of that magnitude were given to players who were drafted and developed by the team that paid them. Veterans rarely get that kind of a contract from a team for which they've never played. It still happens. Kirk Cousins has twice gotten major contracts on the open market. The Vikings made him the highest-paid quarterback in the NFL in 2018, when he left Washington. The Falcons paid him $45 million per year two years ago. Much of what happens in early 2027 depends on how things go this year. The better his season, the more he'll make. And the more likely the Bucs will be to find a way to tag him. That's where the dog starts chasing its tail. The more likely he'll break the bank as a free agent, the more likely it becomes that the Bucs will tag him. Then there's the possibility that Mayfield's decision to take a flamethrower to the Bucs wasn't just Baker being Baker but a strategic move aimed at making them want to move on. If so, the Buccaneers had better have a good plan for finding a quarterback in 2027. The current options on the roster are Jake Browning, Jalon Daniels, and Connor Bazelak. Which confirms the point. If Mayfield leaves, they'll need to find a new starter. There's a long way before we get there. But there isn't. Once the season gets rolling, it'll be over before we know it. And then the question will be whether it's over for Mayfield in Tampa.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: DeAndre Hopkins to join Georgia Tech coaching staff
summary: After spending some time with the Patriots during training camp, DeAndre Hopkins has found a more permanent job in coaching.
full_text: After spending some time with the Patriots during training camp, DeAndre Hopkins has found a more permanent job in coaching. Per Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports, Georgia Tech is expected to hire Hopkins as a member of the program’s offensive staff. After departing New England’s training camp, Hopkins has spent time this week visiting with the team. George Godsey, Georgia Tech’s offensive coordinator, was previously Hopkins’ OC with the Texans from 2015-2016. Godsey was also on last year’s Ravens staff as tight ends coach when Hopkins was with Baltimore. If this is indeed the end for Hopkins as an NFL player, he’ll finish with 1,006 receptions for 13,295 yards with 85 touchdowns in 195 games over 13 seasons. He had 22 catches for 330 yards with two TDs with the Ravens last year.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Ravens activate LB Adisa Issac, CB Bilhal Kone
summary: The Ravens got a pair of defensive players back from the physically unable to perform list on Friday.
full_text: The Ravens got a pair of defensive players back from the physically unable to perform list on Friday. They announced that linebacker Adisa Isaac and cornerback Bilhal Kone have both been cleared to start practicing with the team at training camp. Isaac will be hoping for better health in his third season. The 2024 third-round pick only played in four games as a rookie due to a hamstring injury and he missed all of last season after dislocating his elbow. Kone was a sixth-round pick last April, but didn't play in the regular season because he tore his ACL and MCL in the Ravens' first preseason game last summer.
author: Josh Alper

title: Tua Tagovailoa: I feel great, limited practices are a precaution
summary: Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa spoke about the back issue that has limited him in practice this week for the first time on Friday.
full_text: Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa spoke about the back issue that has limited him in practice this week for the first time on Friday. Tagovailoa said at a press conference that he started feeling "just some tightness" in his back sometime last week and that led to the decision for him to sit out Wednesday's opening practice of training camp. Tagovailoa has done limited practice work the last couple of days and said that the current plan is to continue taking things slow because of where they are in the calendar. "I think just right now, it's just a precaution thing early on in camp and then we’ll work through that ," Tagovailoa said. "I feel great right now. Like I said, it feels good to be out there with the guys, be able to throw, continue to hear the plays, get in the huddle with the guys. All of that.” Tagovailoa said this is the first time he's experienced the back issue and that he's done a lot of work in a pool with the training staff to relieve the tension he's been under. As of now, there's no timetable for when Tagovailoa will move up to a full practice workload but there wasn't much sign of concern from him or head coach Kevin Stefanski about how long it will be until that time arrives.
author: Josh Alper

title: J.J. Watt will replace Tony Romo during his CBS leave
summary: With CBS placing No. 1 NFL analyst Tony Romo on leave following a recent arrest for suspicion of operating while intoxicated, his spot needs to be filled.
full_text: With CBS placing No. 1 NFL analyst Tony Romo on leave following a recent arrest for suspicion of operating while intoxicated, his spot needs to be filled. CBS has announced that it will be filled by J.J. Watt. The move will result in further adjustments to the full roster. The slate was already going to change, given that Jason McCourty signed an exclusive deal with ESPN and exited his role as a game analyst at CBS. Watt, a three-time NFL defensive player of the year, normally serves on the No. 2 team at CBS, with Ian Eagles. Watt will work with Jim Nantz until Romo's leave of absence ends. It's unclear when that will happen. Per CBS, Romo will be on leave "until further notice."
author: Mike Florio

title: 49ers sign TE Josiah Deguara, WR Trenton Irwin
summary: The 49ers have brought in a pair of offensive players.
full_text: '' The 49ers have brought in a pair of offensive players. San Francisco announced on Friday that the club has signed tight end Josiah Deguara and receiver Trenton Irwin to one-year deals. Deguara appeared in 12 games with two starts for the Cardinals last season, catching three passes for 21 yards with a touchdown. Since entering the league as a third-round pick in 2020 with Green Bay, he’s appeared in 77 games, catching 53 passes for 471 yards with three TDs. Irwin has played most of his career with Cincinnati, but has also spent time with Miami, Carolina, Jacksonville, and the Jets. He’s appeared in 41 career games — all for the Bengals — catching 46 passes for 601 yards with five touchdowns. He last appeared in a regular-season game in 2024. As corresponding moves, the 49ers have waived cornerback Derrick Canteen and waived tight end Tanner McLachlan with an injury designation.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Kellen Moore: Chris Olave's new deal is awesome for him, our team
summary: On Thursday, the Saints agreed to a four-year extension with Chris Olave, ending the receiver’s brief hold-in as he sought a new deal.
full_text: On Thursday, the Saints agreed to a four-year extension with Chris Olave, ending the receiver’s brief hold-in as he sought a new deal. Head coach Kellen Moore called it “ awesome for our team, awesome for Chris ” in his Friday press conference. “Just awesome for what he’s gone through in his career, the success he’s had, also the things he’s had to navigate,” Moore said. “At the end of the day, when everyone is shooting for the same goal, it’s a matter of time before it gets figured out. Sometimes the business part takes a little precedence, which is fine. And I think everyone’s really, really excited for where this thing’s going.” The No. 11 overall pick of the 2022 draft, Olave has eclipsed 1,000 yards in three of his four seasons since entering the league out of Ohio State. In 2025, Olave set career highs in receptions (100), yards (1,163), and touchdowns (nine). In all, he’s caught 291 passes for 3,728 yards with 19 TDs in 55 games.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Travis Hunter feels lighter on his feet after putting on 10 pounds
summary: Travis Hunter's mixture of size and speed made him a two-way player at Colorado and it led the Jaguars to trade up to take him with the second overall pick of the 2025 draft, but that didn't stop him from changing his body ahead of his second NFL season.
full_text: Travis Hunter's mixture of size and speed made him a two-way player at Colorado and it led the Jaguars to trade up to take him with the second overall pick of the 2025 draft, but that didn't stop him from changing his body ahead of his second NFL season. Hunter spent his first full pro offseason working his way back from the knee injury that ended his rookie season and he told reporters on Friday that he also worked to bulk up. Hunter said that he put on 10 pounds while working out and that initial concerns that he might hamper his speed turned out to be unwarranted. "I was scared at first . I was like ‘Oh, dang, I ain’t never played at this weight. I’m gonna feel heavy, not going to be able to do what I do,'" Hunter said. "Training and being able to put those months in, not just on the grass but in the weight room too. Just putting in that work, it made me feel lighter on my feet when I finally touched the grass. I’m just happy to be at this weight and continue to play at this weight." Hunter said he's been clocked at 22.6 miles per hour since putting on the weight, which is a new high for him and he hopes to keep adding speed before resuming his roles as a wide receiver and defensive back in Jacksonville this fall.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bills sign CB D.J. Miller
summary: The Bills announced a pair of roster moves on Friday morning.
full_text: '' The Bills announced a pair of roster moves on Friday morning. They have signed cornerback D.J. Miller to their active roster. Safety Wande Owens was waived in a corresponding move. Miller was undrafted in 2024 and spent time with the Lions and Chiefs before moving on to the UFL the last two seasons. He played for Columbus in 2026 and had 24 tackles, a tackle for loss and three interceptions. He also had two interceptions for Michigan during the 2025 season. Owens was waived with an injury by the Bills ahead of the 2025 season and returned to the team this year.
author: Josh Alper

title: Former NFL Pro Bowl WR DeAndre Hopkins expected to join Georgia Tech's offensive coaching staff
summary: The 34-year-old Hopkins was looking to play in the NFL this season, but instead will be on the Yellow Jackets' sideline
full_text:
NFL Pro Bowl receiver DeAndre Hopkins is set to start the next stage of his career as the 34-year-old is currently expected to join Georgia Tech's offensive staff, sources tell CBS Sports.
Hopkins was around the Georgia Tech facility this week visiting with the team.
The South Carolina native has a long-standing relationship with Yellow Jackets offensive coordinator George Godsey, who was his offensive coordinator for two seasons with the Texans and also worked with him last season in Baltimore.
Hopkins recently concluded a stint working with the New England Patriots , where he spent a few days helping the coaching and personnel staff. He played for New England coach Mike Vrabel when they were with the Titans .
One of the most productive wide receivers of the last decade, Hopkins is a three-time first-team All-Pro and a five-time Pro Bowl selection. He spent the 2025 season with the Ravens , catching 22 passes for 330 yards and two scores.
Earlier this offseason Hopkins indicated in an interview with SiriusXM that he hoped to play a 14th season in the NFL.
"I still got a lot ball left," Hopkins said in June . "But it's not a situation I'm sitting here trying to force or go out and be the regular-season superstar because that's for the young guys, man. That's for the people that they want to develop and give those contracts for the future.
"I know in my position, I'm a utility guy. I'm a special situation kind of guy. I can go out there and beat anybody one on one at any time, but as of lately, I've been a third-down guy. I wasn't used in the red zone last year. But (on) third down, they're gonna put D-Hop in, they're gonna come to me. I don't think that'll change anytime soon."
Hopkins spent a few days around the Patriots staff to explore if he'd be interested in coaching, per Vrabel .
Now, he's set to begin that next career step in Atlanta with the Yellow Jackets.
If Hopkins' NFL career is concluded, the former first-round pick will have totaled 13,295 career receiving yards and 85 touchdowns, ranking in the top 20 all time in both categories. He spent time with the Texans, Cardinals , Titans, Chiefs and Ravens in his career.
Hopkins was an All-American wide receiver at Clemson and is a former four-star recruit from the 2010 recruiting class.
author: Chris Hummer

title: Renner's 2027 NFL Draft scouting series: Ranking the top 10 safeties, including the next Kyle Hamilton?
summary: Tae Johnson has drawn comparisons to the All-Pro Hamilton since arriving at Notre Dame in 2024
full_text:
No one is going to confuse the top of this year's safety class with Caleb Downs anytime soon, but there is a very strong group that could ultimately vie for late first- or early second-round consideration.
This class isn't short on size, either, with numerous prospects below who could pass for linebackers.
Even though the position has been devalued throughout the NFL , I could easily see this class producing a couple more first-rounders like we saw in 2026.
Positional rankings: IOL • S • LB • DT • TE • OT • RB • CB • EDGE • WR • QB
Note: ⭐️ represents each player's 247Sports star rating as a high school recruit
The Kyle Hamilton comparisons have been made since the day the lanky 6-foot-2 safety got to campus at Notre Dame. While Hamilton is obviously a one-of-one who sets an unfair bar, the similarities in their play styles are unmistakable.
Tae Johnson can play deep, slot or in the box without looking out of place. His ultra-long frame allows him to make plays on the ball from behind receivers in coverage while also making him a top-notch tackler in the open field. In his lone season as a starter, he picked off four passes and broke up three more. While Johnson's play strength hasn't come close to Hamilton's yet, the redshirt sophomore still has time to fill out.
With a playmaker's mentality, the biggest thing Johnson needs to clean up is the unnecessary chances he takes. He'll jump routes and take himself out of position more often than he should. That's not unheard of for a one-year starter, though. If he cleans that up, he could easily play his way into the late first round.
Jelani McDonald is the type of well-rounded athlete whose draft stock will always have a high floor. For a taller safety at just over 6-foot-2, his ability to change directions effortlessly is his biggest selling point.
He fits the body type and play style that's becoming en vogue in the slot in the NFL: players with longer wingspans who can bring some weakside linebacker-esque ability in the run game while still mirroring underneath routes. It also helps that he's a physical, sure-handed tackler.
I’d wager a pretty penny that Texas S Jelani McDonald (#4) ends up being a top-50 selection in the 2027 NFL Draft. Possesses a bigger frame (6-2, 200 LBs), good instincts, and overall movement skills. Good football player pic.twitter.com/RhUWESco2M
He was one of many Longhorns who could have been a top-100 pick last spring but opted to return for a potential national title run this season.
KJ Bolden fits perfectly into what's become an early-round Georgia safety pipeline. Malaki Starks, Javon Bullard and Lewis Cine have all gone in the top two rounds over the past five years, and Bolden looks destined to do the same. He was a true freshman starter for the Bulldogs in 2024 and has been nothing but reliable ever since. PFF credits him with allowing only 11 first downs on 744 career coverage snaps.
KJ Bolden coming downhill. True FR continues to make plays pic.twitter.com/P5NRotn2gU
Where he is truly special is ranging on the back end. He can make plays around the line of scrimmage from a two-high alignment or mirror slot verticals in off-quarters. He doesn't have the heft to be a full-time box/slot safety, but if he gets to a ball carrier unblocked, he's an aggressive finisher. Bolden is another safety who could play his way into the first round with a big season.
Ty Benefield spent three years at Boise State, where he broke into the starting lineup midway through his true freshman season before transferring to LSU this offseason.
Even though he's only No. 4 on this list, Benefield is the clear-cut No. 1 from a pure traits perspective. At 6-foot-2 and 208 pounds, he's absurdly twitchy and absurdly violent. Some of the high-end reps he put on tape last year were nothing short of jaw-dropping.
Ty Benefield | SAF | LSU | 6-2, 208 Transfer from Boise State. Runs the alley with violent intentions. Physical downhill enforcer. Flashes in coverage. pic.twitter.com/5JyqkmaZUG
At the moment, however, he doesn't quite put the "safe" in safety. He's too often out of control as a tackler (18.8% career missed tackle rate), and his assignment discipline on the back end is shaky. With the way he plays, though, you'd be silly not to keep him around the line of scrimmage.
Zach Lutmer plays the slot for Iowa, which is always a difficult role to project wholesale to the NFL. With Lutmer's smooth change-of-direction ability and feel for manipulating space, deep safety feels far more likely for him than outside corner at the next level. He's at his best in coverage, where only 13 of his 63 targets last year resulted in a first down.
PICK ‼️ Zach Lutmer gets the ball right back for @HawkeyeFootball 😤 📺: Peacock pic.twitter.com/5n15Nmqymt
While not a true physical presence taking on blocks or shutting down screens, Lutmer is very instinctual against the run. He does his best work knifing around blocks and into the backfield to take down ball carriers. He should be a plug-and-play starter in the slot.
Bray Hubbard is yet another player who blurs the line between safety and linebacker. At a listed 217 pounds, Hubbard is a buffet trip away from being a linebacker. Unsurprisingly, he does his damage as a blitzer and against the run. He's not a zero in coverage, though. He has a great feel for zone and is a stout tackler in space.
Bray Hubbard (S) Alabama ✅ Ideal size at safety 6’2” 215 lbs. ✅ Ball skills with 7 interceptions over the past two seasons ✅ Physicality as a run defender ✅ Quick to read and react ✅ 90.6 run defense grade in 2025 ✅ 82.6 coverage grade in 2025 ✅ Good awareness in… pic.twitter.com/KYiy0KLla3
Any scheme with a defined box safety role or one that likes to bring a safety down into a dime linebacker role will heavily covet Hubbard's skill set next spring.
Faletau Satuala isn't your run-of-the-mill safety at 6-foot-4 ⅝ and 212 pounds. In fact, if Satuala sticks at safety, he'll be the tallest defensive back drafted since 6-foot-4 ¾ Pat Watkins out of Florida State went to the Cowboys in the fifth round in 2006.
Were I advising Satuala, I'd tell him to take a look at Sonny Styles' career arc as a massive safety who switched to linebacker and ended up a top-10 pick. Even now, Satuala's best reps come almost exclusively around the line of scrimmage.
BYU’s Faletau Satuala has been shining early in the Big 12 Championship. He’s been one of the best safeties in the country this season. A name to know for the 2027 NFL Draft. pic.twitter.com/xygfBytuuL
Satuala's movement skills are special for a man that tall, and height is more valuable shutting down underneath windows than it is on the back end. He's only a rising true junior, though, meaning he'll likely use both of his remaining years of eligibility to iron out his best role.
The other Ohio State safety last season, Jaylen McClain got lost in a back seven that saw five of its members get drafted last spring -- three in the top 15. The rising junior was quietly impenetrable in his own right, allowing just 94 yards on 28 targets last year.
While his frame is on the smaller side for the position, he's well built and a gifted all-around mover. The biggest thing he needs to prove this fall is that he can be more of a playmaker after failing to record an interception and totaling only two pass breakups last season.
Peyton Bowen is a former five-star recruit who broke into the starting lineup as a true freshman in 2023. Injuries derailed his sophomore campaign, but he returned to become one of the best safeties in America last fall.
Physically, Bowen is similar to the safety above him on this list in that his frame is smaller than you'd like for a prospect, but his movement skills and physicality more than make up for it. With the way he plays, he's one of the stronger candidates in this top-10 list to move to the slot full-time in the NFL.
When you flip on Jackson Bennee 's tape, it becomes obvious very quickly that the man can flat-out cover.…
author: Mike Renner

title: Dak Prescott 'manifesting' Cowboys' Super Bowl chances; here's the history he has to overcome
summary: Prescott has the stats, the offensive continuity, and the confidence, but he is trying to overcome a piece of NFL history no quarterback has ever conquered
full_text:
Quarterback Dak Prescott's 10-season career with the Dallas Cowboys has been statistically historic.
He, and Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen are the only two quarterbacks in NFL history with 200-plus passing touchdowns and 30-plus rushing touchdowns in their first 10 seasons. In 2025, he broke Tony Romo's franchise passing yards record, and Prescott is now just six passing touchdowns away from surpassing Romo as the Cowboys' all-time leader in that metric, too.
The primary goal left for Prescott to accomplish in his Dallas career is to lift the Vince Lombardi trophy as a Super Bowl champion. That's something he's begun to manifest, rocking a Cowboys Super Bowl XXX champions t-shirt from the 1995 season -- the last time Dallas appeared in and won a Super Bowl -- upon checking into training camp out in Oxnard, California.
"It's just the manifesting thing. ... We want stuff in life a lot of times, but then when people start talking about it, you kind of hesitate. 'Should I say that if they're going to hold me to it?'" Prescott said on Thursday . "Well, absolutely. Playing in this organization, being in it 10 years, going into year 11, I'm not going to shy away from it. When you don't have it, it sucks when you don't get to play for it. When you're watching other teams play in the playoffs, there's nothing worse than that. And so, yeah, I said I'd be the quarterback for the Dallas Cowboys when I was 6 years old and said I'd be in the NFL, and I got here. A lot of things in my life, I said I'd do and I did it. And so why shy away from that now? Why shy away from asking people to hold me to the same standard that I believe that I can accomplish and this team can accomplish?"
Dak Prescott was wearing a Super Bowl XXX shirt as the Cowboys arrived at their training camp hotel. Jan. 28, 1996: Cowboys 27, Steelers 17 Dallas’ last SB trip pic.twitter.com/KyuOPkWEQu
Prescott ranked third last season in passing yards (4,552) while George Pickens ranked third in receiving yards (1,429), Javonte Williams ranked ninth in rushing yards (1,201) and CeeDee Lamb ranked 11th in receiving yards (1,077). Guard Tyler Smith made the Pro Bowl, and right guard Tyler Booker was named to the Pro Football Writers of America's All-Rookie team. Dallas ranked seventh in scoring offense and second in total offense in Brian Schottenheimer's first season as coach. That's why Prescott coined the acronym GOTI -- Greatest Offense There is -- while working out with Dallas' skill position players in Park City, Utah, prior to training camp.
"A lot of times you have a lot of [personnel] turnover. We didn't have much turnover at all on our offensive side. We added some guys and some younger guys are going to have to step up," Prescott said. "So maybe we seasoned the group a little bit and guys are getting older, but we were close to some historic things last year. And when you have the guys [we have], why can't we be? And just yet, let's be the greatest offense there is. You've heard, 'The Greatest Show on Turf,' and all the other different nicknames. ... Each and every one of them loved it or taken pride in it. And that's as cool as anything, is to watch them take pride in and watch them talk about it and say it to each other. It's the way that we've been practicing. We're just going to keep pushing each other."
Not only is Prescott fighting Dallas' 30-season conference championship game drought, the longest active streak in the NFC, he's also fighting historical precedent in his pursuit of Super Bowl glory.
No quarterback has ever won a Super Bowl for a team after failing to appear in a conference title game in his first 10 seasons with a franchise, per CBS Sports Research. The only passer to meet that criteria and lead his team to a Super Bowl appearance was Ken Anderson. In his 1981 NFL MVP season, his 11th year in the league, Anderson's Bengals lost to the San Francisco 49ers .
Prescott, the longest-tenured quarterback with a single franchise in the NFL today, enters his 11th season attempting to defeat historical precedent and achieve Super Bowl glory.
"Why not? And life's about being urgent," Prescott said. "A lot of us want to wait and want to say, 'Oh, we'll do it later,' but what are we really promised? Whether it's football or whether it's life. And so why not now?"
author: Garrett Podell

title: NFL training camp injuries tracker: Latest updates on Nic Scourton, Shemar Stewart, Chris Brazzell II and more
summary: Scourton and Brazzell are out for the season with knee injuries, while Stewart was carted off the practice field Wednesday
full_text:
NFL training camp is typically a time for optimism. Hope abounds that all the changes a team made during the offseason -- whether hiring a new coach, signing players in free agency, acquiring them via trade or selecting them in the draft -- will lead to a better season than the year before.
The one thing every team needs to avoid for that to happen, of course, is injuries. A major injury can derail plans for the entire year, especially if it happens to a key player. Alas, injuries happen every year, and it's important to keep track of who's hurt, when and how the injury happened, and how long they might be sidelined.
With that in mind, consider this your one-stop shop for all the injury news coming out of NFL training camps during July and August.
Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski announced Wednesday that Tagovailoa is working through an injury and will the early portions of training camp. With Tagovailoa sidelined, the Falcons have signed veteran backup Cooper Rush .
Regarding fellow quarterback Michael Penix's status, Stefanski recently said that he still hasn't been cleared for full team activities. Penix is still working his way back from a torn ACL that was sustained during Week 11 of the 2025 season.
The Panthers placed Scourton on injured reserve Friday after he suffered a torn ACL in his right knee on the first day of training camp . Scourton was reportedly in tears as he left the field, and his teammates came over to hug him as he exited.
Head coach Dave Canales said at the time that Scourton would undergo an MRI to determine the severity of the injury, and the results confirmed the second-year edge rusher had torn his ACL.
The Saints were hit with awful news on Wednesday as it appears that Bresee suffered a season-ending ACL tear during Wednesday's practice. A former first-round pick, Bresee has quietly become one of the NFL's best defensive linemen. The Saints will now look to try to find his replacement for the upcoming season.
The 2025 first-round pick's Wednesday practice came to an abrupt end after his leg buckled . Stewart -- who played in just eight games during his rookie season -- was carted off the field shortly after sustaining the injury. According to ESPN , Stewart suffered a hyperextended knee with no ligament damage, which seems like best-case scenario given the initial reporting around the injury.
While the initial plan was for Brazzell to recover without surgery, a second opinion determined that a procedure to repair the moderate LCL tear in his left knee is the best course of action, according to The Athletic . The surgery will force Brazzell to miss his entire rookie season, which is a much longer timeline than the eight weeks that was presented in the immediate wake of his injury. The LCL tear does not appear to be related to the knee issue the third-round pick dealt with leading up to training camp.
The former first-round pick is currently not practicing after experiencing swelling that is related to the PCL injury that he sustained last season. Pearsall is currently being evaluated by the team.
James is expected to miss time after he suffered a rib fracture during Monday's practice. The 49ers have yet to offer a timeline for his possible return.
Mustapha sat out Wednesday's practice as he is dealing with a hamstring strain. Like James, Mustapha's injury occurred during Monday's practice.
McNeill left Friday's practice with a neck injury suffered in a pile-up during 11-on-11 drills, according to the Detroit Free Press . The Lions are already shorthanded in the secondary and can scarcely use an injury up front. McNeil wasn't himself last season after returning from a torn ACL and it's not a great sign to see him banged up early in camp this year.
author: Jared Dubin

title: Rams just dropped a hint about their secret Australian travel plan and it wildly differs from 49ers' plan
summary: The Rams and 49ers will make NFL history in Week 1, but their preparation for the long trip to Melbourne could not be more different
full_text:
For the first time in NFL history, there's going to be a game in Australia. That kicks off Week 1 with the Los Angeles Rams facing the San Francisco 49ers .
One reason it took so long for the NFL to put a game Down Under is the logistics of travel. For the first time, two NFL teams will cross the international dateline to play a regular-season game. The 49ers and Rams kick off at 10:35 a.m. on Friday, Sept. 11 in Australia, which will actually be an 8:35 p.m. ET kickoff on Thursday in the United States thanks to the 14-hour time difference between Melbourne and the Eastern Time Zone. The time change will be even worse for the 49ers and Rams because it will be a 17-hour difference from the Pacific Time Zone, where both teams are based.
This could be a game where the team with the better travel plan could gain a small edge, which makes things interesting because the 49ers and Rams have two completely different philosophies for how they're going to handle the trip.
You could say the Rams revolutionized international travel for NFL teams last season when they decided to arrive in London just one day before their Week 7 game against the Jaguars . The game was played on Oct. 19, and the Rams landed in England that morning. It was an audacious travel plan that no team had ever attempted, and it paid off as the Rams beat Jacksonville, 35-7.
"We were like SEAL Team 6," coach Sean McVay said of the team's trip to London . "We're in and out before you know what happened."
The Rams have actually been pretty secretive about what their Australian travel itinerary is going to look like, but McVay did offer a small hint this week when he was asked if he had finalized the team's travel plans.
"I have, but I'm going to keep that internally," McVay told the media .  "Sorry to disappoint you."
OK, so he offered absolutely nothing there, but he did eventually say that the Australian plan will be similar to the London plan.
"It'll be a similar approach, and really the goal for us is to try to keep guys in as close to a rhythm and routine as possible," McVay said. "This is new to us, even going this far. I trust our group and most importantly, what's going to be best for our players. We always try to take that into consideration."
If the Rams are going to show up the day before the game as they did in London, that would certainly be a bold plan, but it's not as crazy as it sounds.
The flight from Los Angeles to Melbourne is almost 16 hours long and if the Rams want to show up the day before, that means they'd have to leave L.A. on Tuesday, Sept. 8. If they went that route, their flight would land in Melbourne on Thursday, Sept. 10 and then they'd be on the field about 24 hours later for their 10:35 a.m. kickoff on Friday against the 49ers.
Of course, there's also a chance that flying in the day before the game might not work. One big difference between the games in London and Melbourne is that the London game kicks off at 2:30 p.m. local time, while the Melbourne game kicks off at 10:35 a.m. local time. In Australia, players will have to be up early on the day of the game, so it's certainly possible the Rams will leave L.A. on Monday (Sept. 7) for a Wednesday (Sept. 9) arrival in Melbourne.
Either way, it's going to be a short trip for the Rams, and that's clearly what McVay wants. As he noted, the whole point of doing all this travel in such a short window is to keep his guys in "rhythm." Adjusting to the time change in Australia can be difficult, but if you're only there for 24 hours, then you never really have to adjust, which makes it much easier to re-adjust once you fly back home.
As a matter of fact, surviving the flight might end up being one of the biggest challenges. Back in February, Matthew Stafford half-joking said he was worried about how his back would hold up on the long trip.
"Seems like a long flight and I hope my back's not too sore afterwards," Stafford said.
Matthew Stafford gets asked about playing in Australia. Rams are going to need to buy him a sleep number mattress for this flight. #Rams #Australia #49ers pic.twitter.com/QJIsvdf38c
Whether it's one or two days, the Rams' trip will be short and sweet, but the 49ers will be taking a completely different approach.
Although the Rams have been secretive about their travel plans, the 49ers have been an open book. Kyle Shanahan actually revealed exactly what his team is going to do shortly after the schedule came out in May. For the trip Down Under, the 49ers are scheduled to leave San Francisco on Wednesday, Sept. 2 with an expected arrival date of Sept. 4 in Melbourne. That's right, they're heading to Australia a full week before the game.
The 49ers don't want to travel the week of the game because they don't think it will be enough time to acclimate to the 17-hour time difference, so they're leaving a full NINE days before kickoff.
"Usually when you travel with a [16]-hour flight, you don't want to get there the day before because you lose like a whole day there or two and you're just messed up," Shanahan said.
If Shanahan and the 49ers are right, the Rams' plan to arrive in Melbourne just a day or two before the game could backfire on L.A.
"The people we've talked to, you don't feel normal until like the third or fourth day," Shanahan said. "So, we'd like to go out seven days early. But since it takes a day and a half to travel there, we're going to go nine. I think we leave on Wednesday and land on a Friday. And so, then we get there about seven days before our game."
As you can see, these two teams couldn't disagree more on what the optimal travel plan should be for this game.
Even though the 49ers will be Down Under for a week, that hasn't changed Shanahan's feelings about the trip. The 49ers coach made it clear that he isn't a big fan of playing in Australia. Shanahan already complained multiple times this offseason about the fact that his team has to play a game in Melbourne.
That said, there is a chance Shanahan won't make the trip to Australia. The 49ers coach suffered several serious injuries in a car crash on July 14 and although the team is hoping that he'll be able to make the trip to Melbourne, it's not set in stone yet.
"That's not what I've heard from the doctors," 49ers general manager John Lynch said of Shanahan possibly missing the game. "But just like we talked about with players, the timeline kind of takes care of itself. He's got to meet certain markers. But I think the expectation is that long before that he'll be better."
Whether Shanahan is there or not, there are going to be a lot of eyes around the NFL watching the game. With the league set to play several more games in Australia, teams across the league will be curious about which travel plan works best. If the game ends up being a blowout, other franchises will likely look to emulate the travel plan of the winning team.
This is one of two international games that the 49ers will play this season, along with a game in Mexico City, which will set them up to possibly break the NFL record for most miles traveled in a single season. The Rams will be traveling the second-most miles in 2026, so hopefully no one on either team has a fear of flying; otherwise, it could be a long season.

NFL training camps are underway. The newcomers that arrived on their respective teams during the first major waves of free agency and the 2026 NFL Draft have settled into their new environments and will now spend the coming weeks gearing up for their debut seasons in new uniforms.
As teams introduce their rookies to the pros and weave in their veteran pickups, they also continue to look to improve on the periphery. Not every roster hole was filled in March and April, after all, and there is a notable advantage to signing free agents after the NFL Draft: They no longer count against the NFL's compensatory picks formula. That resulted in a slight uptick in the spring, but most of the post-draft signings will continue to trickle in this summer as still-unsigned vets start finding new homes during training camp.
Each of the top 36 players on Pete Prisco's annual free agent ranking has signed, but there is still plenty of quality talent available as the NFL calendar moves through its quietest months. Most recently, Deebo Samuel reportedly agreed on a one-year deal with the San Francisco 49ers worth up to $7 million.
Samuel's return to the Bay Area comes after one year with the Washington Commanders and takes him back to the place where he emerged as a star. With his addition, the 49ers add necessary weapons around quarterback Brock Purdy with Brandon Aiyuk all but certainly done and Ricky Pearsall experiencing lingering effects from last season's knee injury. The signing also leaves eight of the top 100 players still on the market.

title: Ranking the top 100 players in NFL history: Tom Brady, Jerry Rice lead all-time list
summary: Aaron Rodgers enters the 2026 season as one of four active players on our ranking of the greatest players the NFL has ever seen
full_text:
During the 2026 season, Aaron Rodgers will put the finishing touches on a career that will go down as one of the best in the NFL's 107-year history.
It shouldn't come as a surprise that the Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback is one of just four active players to crack the list of the 100 greatest players in NFL history. And while others like Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson may join this list one day, more accomplishments are required to be included among the greatest in league history.
Here was the criteria that went into the latest top 100 NFL ranking ...
100. Adam Vinatieri, K (1996-2019)
Vinatieri is the NFL's career scoring leader and arguably the most clutch kicker in NFL history. He is the only kicker to make two game-winning kicks in the Super Bowl and is the only kicker to make a game-winning field goal in a Super Bowl as time expired.
Vinatieri made two incredibly difficult kicks in snowy conditions during the Patriots' playoff win over the Raiders during New England's first Super Bowl championship run. Five years later, he made five field goals (accounting for each of the Colts' points) during Indianapolis' playoff win over Baltimore.
The first punter to be inducted into the Hall of Fame, Guy was a valued member of each of the Raiders' three Super Bowl championship teams. Guy's brilliance was on display early in Super Bowl XVIII, when he snared a high snap one-handed before booting the ball downfield. Guy was an eight-time Pro Bowler who led the league in yards per punt three times over a four-year span.
98. Derrick Henry , RB (2016-present)
The best running back of this era, King Henry enters the 2026 season ranked 10th all-time in both career rushing yards and total touchdowns. He is one of just nine players to run for over 2,000 yards in a season and holds the most prolific season ever for a running back over the age of 30.
97. Lee Roy Selmon, DE (1976-84)
Tampa Bay's first draft pick, Selmon, spearheaded one of the quickest turnarounds in league history. After losing their first 26 games, the Buccaneers got to within a game of the Super Bowl in just their fourth season. Selmon became that year's Defensive Player of the Year and received his first of six consecutive Pro Bowl nominations.
96. Danny Fortmann, G/LB (1936-43)
George Halas convinced Fortmann to play for his Bears rather than pursue medical school. That worked out well for both men. Fortmann and Halas won three NFL titles together, with the former earning six consecutive All-Pro nods during his Hall of Fame career. Fortmann then served in World War II before embarking on a medical career that included 17 years as the Rams' team physician.
95. Mel Hein, C/DL (1931-45)
Hein remains the only offensive lineman to win league MVP, doing so in 1938. During his 15-year career, Hein was an eight-time first-team All-Pro at center. He won two NFL titles and played for a title seven times.
94. Marcus Allen, RB (1982-97)
The versatile Allen was the first player to record at least 12,000 career rushing yards and at least 5,000 receiving yards. His 145 career touchdowns were the most in league history at the time of his retirement.
Allen's finest moment was in Super Bowl XVIII, when he won MVP honors after scorching Washington for 191 yards and two touchdowns in a 38-9 Raiders rout.
93. Marion Motley, RB/LB (1946-53; 1955)
Motley and teammate Bill Willis were trailblazers; they were the first two Black players to play professional football in the modern era. Following his service in World War II, Motley helped lead the Browns to five consecutive championships. A bruising runner, Motley won two rushing titles and retired with an eye-popping 5.7 yards-per-carry average.
92. Steve Van Buren, RB (1944-51)
Van Buren was the first player to run for over 10 touchdowns in a season (a feat he accomplished three times in his career) and to post multiple 1,000-yard rushing seasons. From 1947-49, Van Buren won three consecutive rushing titles and helped the Eagles capture consecutive NFL championships.
91. Troy Aikman, QB (1989-00)
Aikman doesn't have elite numbers, but he does have three Super Bowl wins, a Super Bowl MVP award and the highest career completion percentage in Super Bowl history with over 60 pass attempts. Aikman's magnum opus was Super Bowl XXVII, when he threw four touchdowns and completed 70% of his throws in Dallas' 52-17 blowout of the Bills. During that postseason, Aikman broke Joe Montana's record for consecutive pass attempts without an interception.
90. Larry Little, G (1967-80)
A key member of the undefeated Dolphins, Little paved the way for the first pair of teammates (Larry Csonka and Mercury Morris) to rush for over 1,000 yards in the same season. His blocking also helped keep Bob Griese clean during Miami's consecutive Super Bowl wins.
89. Troy Polamalu, S (2003-14)
Appropriately nicknamed the "Tasmanian Devil," Polamalu's sixth sense allowed him to make breathtaking plays over his Hall of Fame career. Among his most memorable plays was his fingertip interception against Philip Rivers, anticipating the snap and sacking Kerry Collins during his DPOY season, and his game-clinching pick-six of Joe Flacco in the 2008 AFC title game.
88. Dermontti Dawson, C (1988-00)
Dawson is the greatest center in NFL history, according to Pro Football Focus. After spending his first four seasons in relative obscurity, Dawson earned six consecutive All-Pro nods from 1993-98. He was the best player on the Steelers' 1995 AFC championship team.
87. Bart Starr, QB (1956-71)
Starr was the engine that drove the Packers' championship runs during the 1960s. He was most electric during the playoffs, where he won nine of his 10 starts.
The MVP of the first two Super Bowls, Starr's brilliance during the final moments of the "Ice Bowl" solidified his legacy as an all-time great.
86. Dwight Stephenson, C (1980-87)
While his career was short, Stephenson nonetheless dominated. Some consider him the best center in NFL history. In 1984, his blocking helped Dan Marino record one of the most statistically dominant seasons in pro football history. He was an All-Pro during each of his final four seasons.
85. Buck Buchanan, DT (1963-75)
Buchanan has the distinction of being the first Black player selected first overall in either the AFL or NFL Draft . He was also the first AFL defensive lineman to be inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame.
A Pro Bowler each year from 1964-75, Buchanan helped the Chiefs win three AFL titles and the franchise's first Super Bowl title. Buchanan -- who swatted down a staggering 16 passes during the 1967 season -- recorded the first sack in Super Bowl history when he took down Bart Starr in Super Bowl I.
84. Chuck Bednarik, C/LB (1949-62)
One of the NFL's last two-way players, Bednarik is regarded as one of the hardest hitters in league history (he famously knocked Frank Gifford unconscious during a game in 1960). In the 1960 NFL title game, Bednarik played 58 minutes and made the game-clinching tackle.
83. Rosey Brown, LT (1953-65)
A truly dominant player, Brown was a nine-time Pro Bowler and was tabbed as a first-team All-Pro eight consecutive years. His blocking, which helped clear the way for Hall of Fame halfback Frank Gifford, was a key component of the Giants' first championship season in 1956. Brown missed just four games during his 13-year career.
82. Forrest Gregg, OT (1956; 1958-71)
An invaluable part of the Packers' dynasty, Gregg was a starter on each of Green Bay's five championship teams during the 1960s. He helped provide stellar protection for Bart Starr and created running lanes for Hall of Famers Jim Taylor and Paul Hornung.
81. Mike Ditka, TE (1961-72)
Ditka revolutionized the tight end position. As a rookie, he tallied 1,076 receiving yards and 12 touchdowns while averaging a whopping 19.2 yards per catch. Injuries slowed him down during the middle portion of his career, but he ended his career on a high note by helping the Cowboys capture their first Super Bowl…
