title: Joe Burrow pushes for the Bengals to extend Chase Brown
summary: Joe Burrow has never been shy about telling the Cincinnati Bengals what he thinks they need to do to build a championship-caliber team. The star quarterback has mentioned this 2026 Bengals team being one of the best he’s been a part of to date. On Wednesday, as the Bengals opened training camp for the 2026 […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - JANUARY 4: Chase Brown #30 of the Cincinnati Bengals scores a touchdown during the first quarter of the game against the Cleveland Browns at Paycor Stadium on January 4, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images Joe Burrow has never been shy about telling the Cincinnati Bengals what he thinks they need to do to build a championship-caliber team. The star quarterback has mentioned this 2026 Bengals team being one of the best he’s been a part of to date. On Wednesday, as the Bengals opened training camp for the 2026 season, Burrow offered a particularly strong endorsement of one player who is currently looking for a new contract: running back Chase Brown. Brown is entering the final year of his rookie deal, and while contract talks have been part of the Bengals’ offseason storyline, the 26-year-old running back remains without an extension. Burrow’s latest comments certainly sounded like a quarterback who would like to see that situation changed. “He does everything. He’s a complete back,” Burrow said of Brown. That is arguably the most important part of Burrow’s endorsement. Running backs have become one of the more replaceable positions in the NFL, making it increasingly difficult for players to command major second contracts. But Brown brings something to the table that is harder to replace: the ability to stay on the field in essentially every situation. Burrow specifically pointed to Brown’s ability as a pass protector, his work as a receiver and his explosiveness with the football. He also praised Brown’s ability to make defenders miss, as well as his intelligence and approach to the game. That versatility was on full display in 2025. In his first season as Cincinnati’s full-time starting running back, Brown rushed for 1,019 yards and six touchdowns on 232 carries while adding 69 receptions for 437 yards and five more scores. His 1,456 yards from scrimmage were a career high and represented one of the more productive seasons by a Bengals running back in recent memory. And Burrow believes Cincinnati should take advantage of everything Brown can provide. “I think there’s very few backs in this league that you can say that about,” Burrow said when discussing Brown’s ability to stay on the field for every-down situations. That matters in an offense built around one of the NFL’s best quarterbacks. If Brown can line up in the backfield, motion out as a receiver, pass protect and remain a legitimate rushing threat, defenses cannot simply substitute personnel based on who is on the field. The Bengals can create mismatches without giving away what they are trying to do. That is a valuable weapon for Burrow. And apparently, he wants Cincinnati to use Brown a lot more in 2026. “…a close second is Chase Brown,” Burrow said when discussing his hopes for getting the football into the hands of Cincinnati’s playmakers, with Ja’Marr Chase naturally occupying the top spot. Ja’Marr Chase is obviously the centerpiece of the Bengals’ passing attack, and Tee Higgins remains another major component of the offense. But Burrow making the case that Brown could be next in line for touches speaks to how highly he views the running back. It also makes the contract situation increasingly interesting. The Bengals have already invested heavily in their offensive core, and managing the salary cap will always be part of the equation. Running back contracts are also notoriously difficult to project, particularly when a player is coming off his first 1,000-yard season. Another tricky aspect is the roller coaster of wide-ranging opinions on the value of the running back position around the league. In the 1990s, it was of utmost importance, dwindled a bit in more recent years, but teams are coming back around to see the value of a talented player at the spot. Brown is not simply being asked to carry the football. He has shown that he can contribute as a runner and receiver, while Burrow believes he can be trusted as a pass protector and deployed throughout the formation. That type of versatility potentially gives Brown more value to Cincinnati than a traditional early-down running back. The Bengals will ultimately have to determine what Brown is worth and whether that number fits into their long-term plans. But coming from the franchise quarterback, the message is pretty clear. Joe Burrow wants Chase Brown on the field. He wants the ball in his hands. And based on these comments, he would probably like to see Brown remain in Cincinnati beyond the 2026 season. Now, it is up to the Bengals to decide whether they agree with their quarterback.

title: Ja’Marr Chase discusses competitiveness from Jalen Davis and others in training camp
summary: Everyone was talking about the training camp scuffle from Day 1 of camp for the Cincinnati Bengals. Some people were concerned that Zac Taylor was letting too much go. In reality, it was just players going out and competing against one another to get better. Ja’Marr Chase talked to the media after Day 2 of camp. […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'marr Chase (1) runs a route during the first day of Cincinnati Bengals training camp at the Paycor Stadium practice facility in downtown Cincinnati on Wednesday, July 29, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Everyone was talking about the training camp scuffle from Day 1 of camp for the Cincinnati Bengals . Some people were concerned that Zac Taylor was letting too much go. In reality, it was just players going out and competing against one another to get better. Ja’Marr Chase talked to the media after Day 2 of camp. When asked if he liked seeing that type of fire from the defensive back, “A lot of competitiveness going on, and getting each other better. That’s what I want, exactly what I want. I never seen JD like that. It’s new. I like it. I think it makes them guys practice a little harder,” he said. The “JD” he was referring to is expected nickel corner starter Jalen Davis. It isn’t surprising that a former undrafted free agent who has had to scratch and claw his way on the practice squad and roster would be out there with a bit of a chip on his shoulder. Davis mixed it up with Chase, but also with Mike Gesicki during day one of training camp. The defense is looking to play with more of an edge this season, and Chase is happy about that. The Bengals will head into day three of their training camp on Friday. “That’s what I want … But I like it. I do like it, hell yeah.” – Ja’Marr Chase on yesterday’s scuffle with Jalen Davis #Bengals @WCPO https://t.co/ZGZ0VPTRuc pic.twitter.com/V2tgt6dllB — Caleb Noe (@CalebNoeTV) July 30, 2026

title: Browns legend tapped as team’s best-ever training camp ‘riser’
summary: Everyone loves a good training camp story, none more so than fans of the Cleveland Browns.  Every summer, it seems, there is a little-known player who stands out, usually during the final preseason game, by racking up big stats against an opposing lineup of players who will soon be unemployed. Players like running back Matt […]
full_text: CLEVELAND - SEPTEMBER 19: Wide receiver Joshua Cribbs #16 of the Cleveland Browns runs by wide receiver Jeremy Horne #11 of the Kansas City Chiefs at Cleveland Browns Stadium on September 19, 2010 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Matt Sullivan/Getty Images) | Getty Images Everyone loves a good training camp story, none more so than fans of the Cleveland Browns. Every summer, it seems, there is a little-known player who stands out, usually during the final preseason game, by racking up big stats against an opposing lineup of players who will soon be unemployed. Players like running back Matt Dayes (77 yards on just 8 carries and a rushing touchdown in 2018), or tight end Devon Cajuste, who won over fans that same season as the Browns were featured on Hard Knocks. Sometimes, however, that feel-good story turns out to be an actual NFL player, as in the case of Josh Cribbs. An undrafted free agent out of Kent State in 2005, Cribbs made the coaching staff pay attention by showing his return skills during the preseason. He made the roster that year, and over the course of eight seasons with the Browns, etched his name in the franchise’s record book. That is why he was likely one of the easiest choices for ESPN’s list of unheralded players who made the most of their opportunity during training camp and the preseason : Cribbs joined the Browns in 2005 as an undrafted rookie after a standout career as a quarterback at Kent State. Cleveland moved the dynamic athlete to wide receiver and returner — the latter of which Cribbs had no experience in. Cribbs adjusted quickly to his new positions and earned his way onto the Browns’ active roster after a handful of big returns in the preseason. He went on to set a franchise record with 1,094 return yards as a rookie, earned a six-year extension, and played 10 years in the NFL as one of the most dangerous return specialists in league history. A three-time Pro Bowl selection, Cribbs had three kick return touchdowns in 2007 and 2009. He holds 11 franchise records, according to the team’s website, and had 11 kick returns for touchdowns with the Browns (eight on punts and three on kickoffs), 10,015 kickoff return yards (tops in franchise history and 6,830 yards ahead of second-place Dino Hall), and 2,154 punt return yards (tops in franchise history). He is the team’s all-time leader in combined kickoff and punt return yards (12,169), all-purpose yards (14,065), most kickoff return yards in a single season (1,809 in 2007), most kickoff return touchdowns in a single season (three in 2009), and most all-purpose yards in a single season (2,510 in 2009). Cribbs earned Pro Bowl nods in 2007, 2009, and 2012; was a First Team All-Pro selection in 2009; was chosen to the NFL’s All-Decade Team for the 2000s; and is a member of both the franchise’s Legends Program and the Kent State Sports Hall of Fame. He retired after the 2014 NFL season with the third-most return yards in league history (13,488), third-most kickoff return yards (11,113), and the fifth-most return touchdowns (11). Cleveland plays its three preseason games in just 12 days, starting August 15 against the Chicago Bears and ending on August 27 against the New England Patriots. During that time, someone will give a performance that catches everyone’s attention. With any luck, whoever that is could find himself earning a roster spot and start his journey to being the next Josh Cribbs.

title: Browns HC Todd Monken balancing scheme, talent fit on offense still in training camp
summary: Who is Cleveland Browns HC Todd Monken, and what can be expected of him in his first year as a head coach at the NFL level? A lot can be answered by looking back at Monken’s stops as a coach throughout both college and the pro levels. There is also a lot of data out […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JULY 30: Quincy Williams #5 of the Cleveland Browns shakes hands with head coach Todd Monken during the Cleveland Browns Training Camp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on July 30, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Who is Cleveland Browns HC Todd Monken, and what can be expected of him in his first year as a head coach at the NFL level? A lot can be answered by looking back at Monken’s stops as a coach throughout both college and the pro levels . There is also a lot of data out there, including Monken’s past passing rate , that gives us some indication of what the Browns will look like. On the other hand, at his introductory press conference, Monken gave what we considered a “refreshing take” on whether he is scheme-focused (as many say former HC Kevin Stefanski was) or fits his scheme around the talent he has on the roster: Well, that’s a question I get asked all the time, like what system do you run? What is that? And the way I’ll try to phrase it is to score any way possible. I don’t care what it takes to score, it’s about scoring points. I would hate to put some sort of…any type of connotation as to what system that we are, other than playing to our players’ strengths. I think one of the things that our staff, including myself, have been able to do is take advantage of what a player can do and not what they can’t do. Every player in the NFL is elite, and they all have a trait, at least one trait that allows them to, I don’t want to say this – allows them to function, play at a high level. You just got to find what that is and not try to put a square peg in a round hole, taking advantage of what they do. And I think that’s what we’ve been able to do consistently. At other times during the offseason, Monken has given more of a ‘we are who we are’ style answer to these types of questions. During Week 1 of Cleveland’s training camp, Monken was once again asked about scheme plans now that he’s had time with the players. The Browns head coach noted that they are still figuring things out, including some of it being dependent on what the quarterbacks like: Interesting answer from Browns HC Todd Monken on balancing what he wants to do philosophically vs what his players can do, and figuring that out during training camp. pic.twitter.com/dAaElXtil6 — 𝚂𝚙𝚎𝚗𝚌𝚎𝚛 𝙶𝚎𝚛𝚖𝚊𝚗 (@Spencito_) July 31, 2026 Sounds like Monken has a good idea what he likes as a play caller and coach but needs to identify the starting quarterback, and likely the starting offensive linemen, first before solidifying how Cleveland’s offense will be for the 2026 season. On Thursday, Browns GM Andrew Berry reiterated what Monken has said numerous times about the QB competition : The best-producing quarterback will win the job. The head coach may want to speed that decision up a bit if it is going to move the offensive scheme in a certain direction. What do you think about Monken’s answer during the first week of training camp? Should the team speed up the QB decision so the rest of the offensive scheme can be locked in, or is waiting for the best QB to show himself the best decision? title: Browns training camp: Bad offense or good defense? Todd Monken weighs in
summary: All eyes are on the Cleveland Browns quarterback competition in Berea, with GM Andrew Berry making it clear that only one thing will decide who wins the starting quarterback job. ESPN’s Ben Solak noted how important it is for QB Shedeur Sanders to add a Russell Wilson-type weapon to his arsenal while he tries to […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JULY 29: Head coach Todd Monken of the Cleveland Browns directs a drill during Cleveland Browns Training Camp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on July 29, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images All eyes are on the Cleveland Browns quarterback competition in Berea, with GM Andrew Berry making it clear that only one thing will decide who wins the starting quarterback job . ESPN’s Ben Solak noted how important it is for QB Shedeur Sanders to add a Russell Wilson-type weapon to his arsenal while he tries to fight off veteran QB Deshaun Watson . As noted in our recaps from Day 1 and Day 2 of training camp , the offense, especially the passing offense, has not looked in sync overall. That isn’t totally surprising given the new offensive system, remade offensive line, new but young weapons, and two quarterbacks competing for the starting job. In a video posted by the team’s social media, HC Todd Monken seemed to give credit to the Browns defense for making things tough on the offense so far in training camp: process-oriented and focused on our goals 🔒 pic.twitter.com/MkZJVIW5Ga — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) July 31, 2026 Interesting to note that DE Jared Verse , who wasn’t added to the roster until June, is who Monken has breaking the team huddle at the end of practice. A lot of positives were noted by Monken during this talk, especially that the roster has always been trying to go too fast, too hard. Is it necessarily a good thing that Cleveland’s defense is controlling practice so far? It is too early to tell. Often, different drills are set up to create opportunities for success for each side of the ball, but Monken may not value that as much as other coaches. For now, the Browns defense is making things tough on the Browns offense. That could either bring out the best in Cleveland’s offense down the road or be a sign that the Browns will once again struggle scoring points in 2026. What do you think? title: Where will the Browns offense rank in 2026?
summary: The Cleveland Browns’ offense has struggled to put a consistent product on the field over the last few seasons. The 2026 offense has a few new elements, including some exciting young pass catchers and offensive linemen, but the uncertainty at quarterback makes this group unpredictable.  KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston have an opportunity to produce at a […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns’ offense has struggled to put a consistent product on the field over the last few seasons. The 2026 offense has a few new elements, including some exciting young pass catchers and offensive linemen, but the uncertainty at quarterback makes this group unpredictable. KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston have an opportunity to produce at a high level, and Quinshon Judkins coming back from his injury could really move the needle in the running game. First-round tackle Spencer Fano has more promise than many of the injury-riddled members of the offensive line over the last few seasons. These are all things to get excited about, but the lingering question of Deshaun Watson or Shedeur Sanders leaves some questions. The most likely scenario is that the Browns offense ranks in the middle to bottom half of the league. The best-case scenario is probably in the 10-13 range. The Cleveland offense ranked among the league’s bottom five in most offensive metrics in 2025, so even an improvement to the middle of the pack would represent meaningful progress. Improving an offense in just one season is no easy task, but the team has made meaningful progress toward putting a better product on the field. Let me know what you think in the comments – Where will the Browns offense rank in 2026?

title: Cowboys news: Dak Prescott is more motivated than ever
summary: Time’s moving fast for Dak Prescott, and Cowboys QB is attacking Year 11 with a sense of urgency – Joseph Hoyt, Dallas Morning News Dak Prescott is highly motivated to win. OXNARD, Calif. — Dak Prescott’s decision to wear a Super Bowl shirt on the flight to training camp may have drawn headlines, but it wasn’t exactly a […]
full_text: OXNARD, CALIFORNIA - JULY 30: Dak Prescott #4 of the Dallas Cowboys throws during training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields on July 30, 2026 in Oxnard, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images Time’s moving fast for Dak Prescott, and Cowboys QB is attacking Year 11 with a sense of urgency – Joseph Hoyt, Dallas Morning News Dak Prescott is highly motivated to win. OXNARD, Calif. — Dak Prescott’s decision to wear a Super Bowl shirt on the flight to training camp may have drawn headlines, but it wasn’t exactly a new concept for the veteran quarterback. He’s always been on a mission to manifest. “I said I would be the quarterback for the Dallas Cowboys when I was 6 years old,” Prescott said on Thursday. “I said I would be in the NFL, and I got here. A lot of things I said I’d do, I did it.” There is one difference between the 6-year-old who dreamed of being the quarterback for the Cowboys and the one currently living that existence. Time isn’t exactly on his side. And he knows it. Prescott is entering his 11th season in the NFL. He turned 33 earlier this week , making him the fifth-oldest projected starting quarterback in the NFL. The fourth-round rookie who took the league by storm in 2016 is now the second-oldest player on the team behind 15-year veteran Bryan Anger. Prescott admitted that he thought there would be more chances to go on deep playoff runs after he and the Cowboys finished that 2016 season. They went 13-3 that year and lost by a field goal in the divisional round against Aaron Rodgers and the Green Bay Packers. “We’ll get back here next year,” Prescott recalled thinking. “We’ll block the field goal, or we’ll score and not get in that situation and then you look up and seven, eight years later, you’ve been to the playoffs, you’ve lost some games, some tough games in some brutal ways, and then you get into last season and you think you can control a lot of it and you think your play is ultimately going to be the deciding factor, and I probably had the best year of my career [last year], and we’re not even a playoff team. And then you realize these chances, these opportunities to put teams together that can actually make a run, don’t come often.” Stephen Jones, Cowboys continuing to explore defensive additions at training camp – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com Will the Cowboys bolster their defense before the start of the season? OXNARD, Calif. – In the Cowboys’ opening press conference at training camp, owner/GM Jerry Jones said that he had a discussion with another team’s owner about a trade earlier in the week, although the talks weren’t in a place where something was imminent. He also said he’d be willing to give up a high-draft pick in order to add “firepower” to his roster. Speaking on 105.3 The Fan on Friday, Cowboys COO/co-owner Stephen Jones said Dallas is exploring different possibilities to add, specifically on defense. “We’ve got several things that we’re considering right now, some of it trades, some of it signing guys,” Jones said. “A lot of these older players who have still got some tread on the tires can come in here and help you. It may come in the form of a trade; it may come in the form of a veteran signing as you move into camp.” When it comes to what kind of players Jones and the Cowboys are looking to add to the roster, Jones hinted towards them being able to contribute as starters. “I’d be surprised if the starting players on this defense don’t change over time,” Jones said. “We’re always looking to be better, we’ll continue to monitor this.” Cowboys training camp observations: Dak Prescott is thinking big – Jon Machota, The Athletic The first two days of training camp provided much to talk about. Prescott-Pickens connection The rapport that standout wide receiver George Pickens has had with Prescott early in camp is ahead of where the two were at this time last season. Pickens and Prescott look similar to what we’ve seen from CeeDee Lamb and Prescott entering previous camps. One of the highlight plays of the first two days was a beautiful ball Prescott threw over the top of cornerback Caelen Carson directly into the hands of Pickens running up the left sideline. There’s no tackling in these practices, but the play would’ve gone for at least 30 yards in a game. Pickens’ personality has been on display after catches such as that one. He has celebrated after some of his notable plays as if it were a regular-season game. Some might have wondered how Pickens would handle camp while playing under the franchise tag. He appears to be pleased with his current situation. “I left it up to my agent,” Pickens said after Thursday’s practice. “Even when we were (several) months from training camp, I was already thinking about ball. I was already training. I kind of leave (contract discussions) to the people who can do that for me. I just make catches and make plays and be a playmaker.” Cowboys owner Jerry Jones emphasized Tuesday that Pickens could be a Cowboy for the rest of his career. Pickens’ thoughts on those comments? “Super excited,” he said. “I’m always super happy when someone thinks highly of me, so shout out to Jerry.” Caleb Downs making waves at Cowboys training camp: ‘It’s about being great today’ – Patrik Walker, DallasCowboys.com The rookie hasn’t wasted any time proving his was worth a first-round pick. OXNARD, Calif. — Caleb Downs is getting his first real taste of what it means to be an NFL player and he can’t get enough. The rookie 11th-overall pick has now experienced rookie minicamp, OTAs and mandatory minicamp, but none of those compare to what he’ll experience in his first-ever training camp with the Dallas Cowboys. The rubber meets the road in Oxnard, and the physicality is already ratcheted way up, as ordered by head coach Brian Schottenheimer. With the first two days of practice of his belt and padded practice firing up on Monday, Downs says bring it on. “Yeah, I feel like every day things slow down just a little bit, and that’s how it’s supposed to be,” the former Ohio State superstar said. “It’s always positive to have the spring behind me, to be able to learn from what I did in the spring and make the adjustments that I need to and learn what I need to focus on. So, I’m excited for it, and we keep going from here.” Schottenheimer continues to praise the fact that Downs “never makes the same mistake twice”, and the fact he lives in the playbook certainly helps that remain true. But it’s also his ability on the field, and the fact he craves the game as much as he does studying it. “Yeah, I mean, honestly, I’m a football player,” he added. “So, 7-on-7 summer workouts, when there’s no pads, that’s good, but I like the real thing. I’m excited for when we put pads — I want to do everything like that, and I’m looking forward to it. “I mean, it’s [also] just film study. It’s the same thing that I’ve been doing since I was a kid, just making sure that I’m watching everything that I need to watch, going from there and making sure that whenever it comes back, I’ll make the play.” Daily discussion question: What is the biggest thing you need to see from camp at this point?

Stephen Jones stirred the pot on Friday Cowboys EVP Stephen Jones took to the radio airwaves of 105.3 The Fan on Friday and in his appearance he stirred the pot of rumors. The Cowboys have been connected to Maxx Crosby all offseason basically, but the fire that had dimmed had a dumping of kerosene early this week when Jerry Jones fielded a quesiton about the Raiders’ star pass rusher during Dallas’ press conference to open traiing camp. Stephen’s words on The Fan were not exactly pointed, but he basically said the Cowboys are interested in something . Stephen Jones on @1053thefan : "We've got several things that we're considering right now, some of it trades, some of it signing guys. A lot of these older players who have still got some tread on the tires can come in here and help you. It may come in the form of a trade, it may… — Tommy Yarrish (@tommy_yarrish) July 31, 2026 Stephen Jones on @1053thefan : "I'd be surprised if the starting players on this defense don't change over time. We're always looking to be better, we'll continue to monitor this." — Tommy Yarrish (@tommy_yarrish) July 31, 2026 Stephen also left room for the possibility of bringing in a veteran. We know that there are players out there like Von Miller who would relish the opportunity to play for Dallas , so maybe somebody of that variety. Do you think the Cowboys are legitimately cooking something up? Or do you think this is just talk on an off day? Let us know in the comments below.

title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 44
summary: It is Day 44 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: DALLAS, TX - DECEMBER 26: Robert Newhouse #44 of the Dallas Cowboys carries the ball against the Chicago Bears during the NFC Divisional Playoff Game December 26, 1977 at Texas Stadium in Dallas, Texas. Newhouse played for the Cowboys from 1972-83. (Photo by Focus on Sport/Getty Images) | Getty Images It is Day 44 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. We have reached reach Day 44 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit a playoff control game from one of the most complete teams in Cowboys history. Dallas hosted the Chicago Bears in the NFC Divisional Round after finishing the regular season 12-2, and this was the first step in what became the Cowboys’ march to Super Bowl XII. The Bears had Walter Payton, the league’s MVP and rushing champion, but Dallas had the Doomsday Defense, Roger Staubach, Tony Dorsett, and too much playoff polish. Monday, December 26, 1977 — 2:00 p.m. ET Texas Stadium, Irving, Texas Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 37, Chicago Bears 7 Dallas set the tone early with the run game. Staubach hit Dorsett for 32 yards, which set up Doug Dennison’s two-yard touchdown run and gave the Cowboys a 7-0 lead. That opening sequence mattered because it immediately put Chicago in chase mode, something the Bears were not built to do. They wanted the game in Payton’s hands. Dallas made it about Bob Avellini having to throw into a defense that was waiting for mistakes. The Cowboys kept building in the second quarter. Staubach connected with Drew Pearson for 31 yards, then found Billy Joe DuPree for a 28-yard touchdown to make it 14-0. Efren Herrera added a 21-yard field goal, and Dallas led 17-0 at halftime. Chicago had a chance to cut into the lead before the break, but Charlie Waters intercepted Avellini in the end zone. That play captured the whole afternoon, the Bears would get a little movement, then Dallas would slam the door. The game fully broke open on the first play of the second half. D.D. Lewis intercepted Avellini, and Dallas immediately turned the short field into a Tony Dorsett 23-yard touchdown run. On Chicago’s next possession, Avellini lost a fumble, and Herrera turned that into another field goal. Within minutes, the Cowboys had stretched a 17-0 lead to 27-0, and the game was effectively finished. Dorsett added a seven-yard touchdown run later in the third quarter, Herrera kicked another field goal in the fourth, and Dallas led 37-0 before Chicago finally avoided the shutout on a 34-yard Avellini touchdown pass to Steve Schubert. By then, the only question was how dominant the final numbers would look. Dallas had controlled the ball, controlled the line of scrimmage, and most of all they controlled Payton. Andy there was the biggest story of the day. Payton had rushed for 1,852 yards during the regular season, but the Cowboys held him to 60 yards on 19 carries. Chicago finished with seven turnovers, including four Avellini interceptions with Waters making three of them, while Lewis added another. For a Bears team making its first playoff appearance since the 1963 championship season, Dallas turned the moment into a lesson in postseason football. This game belongs on the countdown because it shows the 1977 Cowboys at their most ruthless. Chicago arrived with the league MVP and a six-game winning streak. Dallas turned that into a 30-point playoff blowout. One week later, the Cowboys beat Minnesota 23-6 in the NFC Championship Game, then defeated Denver 27-10 in Super Bowl XII. This was the first postseason hammer blow in that title run, and it was a really big hammer. #Cowboys vs #Bears 1977 Divisional Round Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 37, Chicago Bears 7 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/4AkON0JTHd — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) July 30, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game Charlie Waters set an NFL playoff record with three interceptions in one game. Dallas forced seven Chicago turnovers overall, turning a dangerous Bears team into a one-dimensional mess. title: Cowboys RB usage through two days of practice has been fun
summary: The Dallas Cowboys completed their second practice of training camp on Thursday afternoon, still without the pads on which will have to wait. Unpadded practices always sway in favor of the offense in general and particularly the pass-catching skill position players, and this was mostly the case on Thursday. With so much discussion about fixing […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - DECEMBER 14: Dallas Cowboys running back Javonte Williams (33) runs through the line of scrimmage during the game between the Dallas Cowboys and the Minnesota Vikings on December 14, 2025 at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Matthew Pearce/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys completed their second practice of training camp on Thursday afternoon, still without the pads on which will have to wait. Unpadded practices always sway in favor of the offense in general and particularly the pass-catching skill position players, and this was mostly the case on Thursday. With so much discussion about fixing the defense and the star power in the passing game on offense, the running game has gone under the radar. Even from a franchise that has prided itself on running backs for nearly as long as they’ve existed, and with a head coach that came out of the gates in his debut season last year talking about wanting to run the football. The team returns a starting running back that just set career highs in carries, yards, touchdowns, yards per attempt, and rushing success rate, but the superstar-fueled passing game is still overshadowing the ground attack. Day two of practice showed some of the specific areas the team’s running back usage can improve in year two of Brian Schottenheimer calling plays and Klayton Adams as OC. The surprise of the day from the opening practice was second-year draft pick Phil Mafah getting RB2 carries, and this continued on Thursday with Mafah hitting this home run off-tackle. Phil Mafah big run untouched pic.twitter.com/eI5PpglJSW — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) July 30, 2026 Mafah is competing with another second-year player in Jaydon Blue for the RB2 role, and also for the second day in a row, Blue had a big run through the defense. Jaydon Blue breaking out into the open for the second day in a row pic.twitter.com/vsJv4CXmqi — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) July 30, 2026 It remains to be seen just how many reps there will be for Blue, Mafah, or even a dark horse candidate that can emerge behind Williams as the starter. Last season, the Cowboys had 362 total carries from four running backs in Williams, Malik Davis, Blue, and Miles Sanders. Williams accounted for 69% of these carries as the lead back. Interestingly enough, that stat is incredibly telling when it comes to how Schotty wants to scheme his backfield over a larger sample size as well. In his first year as offensive coordinator back in 2023, the Cowboys had nearly the same number of RB carries at 364, and Tony Pollard came in at 69% of the share as well with 252 of them. The 2024 season is a slight outlier with a lower total carry total of 326, and a higher lead-back percentage use of 72% for Rico Dowdle, but among a lot of reasons this was the case, Ezekiel Elliott not being a viable option as the RB2 with his 74 carries was a main one. While dominating almost 70% of a team’s season-long carries is a big deal, 30% of a full season’s work out of the backfield is no laughing matter either. Very early on in camp, the Cowboys are seeing positive signs from the players they can use in this 30% space, but also are looking at expanding even more areas for the ultra-reliable Williams to do even more. Brian Schottenheimer said they wanted to get Javonte Williams involved in the screen game. Here’s a good example. pic.twitter.com/KnOuhJnFBx — Joseph Hoyt (@JoeJHoyt) July 30, 2026 Williams left a lot of opportunity in the pass game on the field a year ago, and the Cowboys short passing game as a whole suffered because of it. With the amount of deep coverage attention that Pickens and Lamb should draw, as well as their increasing ability to win in the short pass game themselves, spreading the ball around to running backs through the air truly could be the last element that makes the Cowboys offense nearly unstoppable in 2026. Another thing to love about the screen play above to Williams is that Tyler Booker is the one out in front to block for it. When it comes to under the radar things concerning the Cowboys run game, having a right guard going into year two as the first-round pick tasked with the unenviable job of replacing Zack Martin as a rookie is a massive one, and continuing to keep an eye on how much Booker has improved as a road-grader for these backs will be especially fun once padded practices begin. Javonte Williams with a nice run. pic.twitter.com/0DqB4cEKsq — Calvin Watkins (@calvinwatkins) July 30, 2026 The path of least resistance for any team in the NFL to win games is with a dominant run game. All four teams around the NFC East have their own reasons to believe in what they’re doing out of the backfield heavily for 2026, but the Cowboys have wasted no time showing off their balance as well as RB depth in Oxnard.

title: Cowboys 2026 roster rundown: OLB Malachi Lawrence
summary: Malachi Lawrence may be one of the most unheralded first-round picks in Cowboys history. With Caleb Downs drawing so much attention, Lawrence is flying under the radar as a rookie. But with likely a key role at a spotlight position on defense, Lawrence is sure to generate hype this August and hopefully in the regular […]
full_text: Malachi Lawrence may be one of the most unheralded first-round picks in Cowboys history. With Caleb Downs drawing so much attention, Lawrence is flying under the radar as a rookie. But with likely a key role at a spotlight position on defense, Lawrence is sure to generate hype this August and hopefully in the regular season. Background Years in NFL: 0 Acquired by: 2026 1st-round pick Lawrence had a full five-year, redshirt run at Central Florida as a pass rusher. His career-high in sacks was 7.5 in 2023, but last season he earned First-team All-Big 12 honors with seven sacks, 11 tackles for loss, three pass deflections, and two forced fumbles for the Knights. A strong showing at the scouting combine boosted his stock, pushing Lawrence into late first/early second-round consideration for the 2026 NFL Draft. With two firsts last April, the Cowboys were poised for an exciting Thursday night. Coming off a dreadful defensive year, that was Dallas’ assumed focus for its rookie class. Improving the pass rush was also a top priority, with several scenarios that could have an edge player going at the 12th-overall pick. But as it turned out, blue-chip safety Caleb Downs fell out of the top 10 and was grabbed by the Cowboys after a quick move up to the 11th pick. Twelve picks later, we were still celebrating the Downs pick by the time Dallas was back on the clock. With Downs helping the secondary, a pick for the front seven felt likely. Lawrence was among the top possibilities, though some thought it could be Auburn’s Keldric Faulk, or Clemson products Peter Woods or T.J. Parker. There were also a few intriguing offensive prospects like WRs KC Concepcion or Omar Cooper Jr., or OT Caleb Lomu. But in a fitting use of a pick they obtained in the Micah Parsons trade, the Cowboys went with the pass rusher in Lawrence. Contract Status Years Left: 4 2026 Cap Hit: $3.68 million During the 2029 season, Dallas will likely have to make two fifth-year option decisions on Downs and Lawrence. Ultimately, it’s a nice problem to have if both guys turn into defensive leaders. We’ll also be at the end of Dak Prescott’s current contract, so it’s hard to project what the Cowboys’ salary cap landscape will be. 2026 Projections Role: Rotation OLB Roster Chance: 100% We already know that Lawrence will have a big share in the pass-rushing rotation, even as a rookie. How Dallas divides the snaps between Lawrence, Rashan Gary, and Donovan Ezeiruaku is one of the big questions ahead of 2026. But they will all see plenty of work, hopefully with enough mutual success to be labeled a “three-headed monster” by the end of the season. As far as starting jobs, Gary is the most likely for early-down work as a veteran and a run stopper. How Ezeiruaku and Lawrence perform in run defense will probably decide who gets the most starts between them. Last year, Ezeiruaku was surprisingly good there despite his size. Being a first-round pick won’t give Lawrence any extra consideration for starts or playing time, as Ezeiruaku has plenty of potential and long-term consideration as well. While this top three feels pretty certain, we can’t dismiss guys like James Houston and Sam Williams, either. Lawrence is still a rookie and has plenty to learn, giving these veterans a chance to impress early and perhaps claim their own shares in the rotation. Though we’re rightfully concerned about whether or not there’s a true sack artist in this bunch, there are plenty of guys who could produce in a well-designed and executed defensive scheme. Lawrence may not be getting the kind of fanfare that most first-round picks are accustomed to, but it’s all speculative in the offseason. If the rookie gets his flowers now and especially starting in September, it will be far more beneficial to him and the Cowboys going forward. In a year full of shiny new toys on defense, Lawrence will get every opportunity to show his stuff as one of the top newcomers. title: Cowboys gave an unusual challenge to an important player
summary: NFL football is as much a game of mental aptitude and psychological warfare as it is a showcase of raw physical ability. And for some players, those responsibilities grow large. That’s the case for green-dot linebacker DeMarvion Overshown. During the Dallas Cowboys’ training camp session on Thursday, his green-dot responsibilities put him under the microscope […]
full_text: NFL football is as much a game of mental aptitude and psychological warfare as it is a showcase of raw physical ability. And for some players, those responsibilities grow large. That’s the case for green-dot linebacker DeMarvion Overshown. During the Dallas Cowboys’ training camp session on Thursday, his green-dot responsibilities put him under the microscope as head coach Brian Schottenheimer and defensive coordinator Christian Parker orchestrated a little technological malfunction that provided a test for their young linebacker. on DeMarvion Overshown: in the #Cowboys first practice, Christian Parker pretended his headset went out (but Overshown thought he was serious — CP and Schotty having planned the deception to test his green dot ability). "Overshown immediately made the right [play] call." — Patrik [No C] Walker (@VoiceOfTheStar) July 30, 2026 During team periods, the defense was trying to shut down a potent Cowboys offense when the coaching staff got a little fancy. Right in the middle of a crucial pre-snap sequence, Overshown’s radio went dead. It wasn’t a glitch or his battery dying. It was pure sabotage. The coaches purposely cut the communication line to see how his linebacker would handle himself. No communication. No problem. With the time winding down and the offense shifting into formation, Overshown did not panic. No distress signals to the sideline. Instead, he took complete command of the situation. He got into the exact call he was supposed to. He had gone through this repeated times with the coaches in meetings, so there was no need to improvise. He knew exactly what he needed to do. By the time the ball was snapped, the entire unit was perfectly aligned, ready for action. From Schottenheimer… “D-Mo got to the exact call that he was supposed to, which is what you expect. D-Mo was outstanding in getting us to the call we needed to be in.” This kind of poise under pressure is exactly why the Cowboys have such high expectations for Overshown, despite a career heavily disrupted by injuries. After missing his entire 2023 rookie season with a torn ACL, the former third-round pick flashed elite potential in 2024, racking up 90 tackles, five sacks, and a deflected-to-himself interception that he returned for a touchdown. He did this in just 13 games before a devastating multi-ligament knee injury ended his breakout season early. He spent the majority of last year rehabbing that knee. Now, entering a contract year where he is completely healthy, this season represents a massive, career-defining moment for the young linebacker. He is playing not just for a permanent starting role as a defensive leader, but also to prove his resiliency and add a little financial job security in the NFL. This little mind game was a good first test to see how Overshown would handle himself without a safety net. The Cowboys defense was notorious for in-game breakdowns last season, so it is critical to make sure their leaders have got their affairs in order and can get their troops organized, and do so in a hurry. By intentionally creating a chaotic environment, the coaches learned that Overshown has the mental fortitude necessary to be an on-field general. Coaches try to make things as easy as possible for their players by providing the tools they need, but there is only so much direction available. Sometimes, they have to think for themselves and make split-second decisions. Training camp will tell them where they are with certain elements of the defense, and on Thursday, they learned that radio silence will not slow down their rising star linebacker. The communication may have cut off, but the message was received loud and clear, and that message is that Overshown is completely dialed into his new role on the defense.

summary: After a long offseason, the Dallas Cowboys are back to football in Oxnard, California. To make things even more exciting, Jerry Jones spent a rather large portion of his state of the […]
full_text: Jul 28, 2026; Oxnard, CA, USA; Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones at training camp opening press conference at River Ridge Playing Fields. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect After a long offseason, the Dallas Cowboys are back to football in Oxnard, California. With all the new players and coaches, this is one of the more exciting training camps for Cowboys fans in quite some time. To make things even more exciting, Jerry Jones spent a rather large portion of his state of the union press conference talking about the desire to trade future assets for a key defensive piece. During the conversation, Las Vegas Raiders edge rusher Maxx Crosby’s name was mention, and the rumor mill has been swirling ever since. It’s no secret that Jerry Jones is infatuated with Crosby and his impact on the field. The rumor mill picked up even more late on Thursday, when it was reported by Nick Harris that Doctor Dan Cooper, the Cowboys’ team doctor, had an interesting meeting with Jerry and Stephen Jones in a private setting at the conclusion of the Cowboys’ second practice. Something worth noting from after practice: Jerry Jones and Stephen Jones flagged down Dr. Dan Cooper (white polo & hat) for a 5-10 minute conversation. Looked way more in-depth than just talking about P.J. Locke's hyperextended knee, but no way to know. pic.twitter.com/X5VyYE73z4 — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) July 30, 2026 We should be clear here, everything that follows is speculation and a game of connecting the dots, but here goes. Doctor Cooper was one of the medical specialist who examined and reviewed the injury to Crosby’s knee, that ultimately led to the trade with the Baltimore Ravens to fall through. After Jerry’s comments about the Cowboys not being “out” on trading for Crosby, and the mysterious meeting at the end of Thursday’s practice, Cowboys fans can wonder what that conversation was about. Given the smoke surrounding the Cowboys past interest in Crosby, and Jerry’s comments to kickoff training camp, the gas has been poured on the Crosby-to-Dallas fire. This meeting with Doctor Cooper just adds to it. Could the Jones’ just be asking Dr. Cooper his thoughts on P.J. Locke’s hyper-extended knee? Or were they asking questions about Crosby’s knee ahead of making a push for the Raiders star edge rusher? Again, this is just speculation, but we’d love to know your thoughts.

title: Cowboys news: Recapping training camp practice #2
summary: Dallas Cowboys Training Camp Day 2 Notes: Javonte Williams is being asked to do something he didn’t do enough of last year and more – Mauricio Rodriguez, A to Z Sports The Cowboys offense has shined through two training camp practices. Javonte Williams as a pass catcher changes things There has been a clear focus […]
full_text: Dallas Cowboys Training Camp Day 2 Notes: Javonte Williams is being asked to do something he didn’t do enough of last year and more – Mauricio Rodriguez, A to Z Sports The Cowboys offense has shined through two training camp practices. Javonte Williams as a pass catcher changes things There has been a clear focus by the Cowboys in these first couple of practices to develop the screen game, and that could be huge for the offense. Granted, screens can get predictable if you go about them the wrong way. Cowboys fans, media, and content creators know that all too well from years past. However, it has been a long time since running backs posed a legitimate threat in Dallas’ passing game, and that might change in 2026. The Cowboys are trying to get Williams more involved as a receiver. One play stood out from Thursday’s practice: Dak Prescott found Williams on a screen, and safety Caleb Downs came crashing down as a blitzer. The full view wasn’t available, but it looked like Downs was caught off guard by the play. Here’s the thing about Williams as a pass catcher: if he can contribute in the receiving game, the value you’re getting out of him goes up a notch. Last season, as good as Williams was running the ball, he was a non-factor through the air. Out of 51 running backs with minimum targets, Williams ranked dead last in EPA per target and dead last in yards per route run. His success rate came in 48th out of 51. He was essentially a checkdown catcher who gave you a completion but no damage after the catch. Practice Points: Thursday’s quick observations – DallasCowboys.com What stood out in Thursday’s practice? OXNARD, Calif. – Back at it for Thursday’s Day 2 of training camp, the Cowboys put together another spirited practice — even without pads coming on. The offense continued to make plenty of plays, much like it did on Wednesday, but the defense responded and helped even things out. This team entered camp relatively healthy, which makes every rep that much more important as players try to get on the field as much as possible. Here are some quick observations from the Cowboys’ staff writers. 4-2-88: The middle of the field has been friendly grounds for Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb to connect over the years, and the same was true on Thursday’s practice. Lamb was open on several occasions, and Prescott found him each time, allowing Lamb to turn the corner and finish plays that would’ve gone for chunk gains. Prescott was also able to get Jonathan Mingo involved in the middle of the field for a big gain, as Mingo fights for a spot on the 53-man roster. – (Tommy Yarrish) Adding Spice : After saying he’s feeling better than he did following his first foot surgery, Cowboys CB DaRon Bland had a strong practice highlighted by jumping a quick short route and breaking up a pass intended for Brevyn Spann-Ford. From there, you didn’t notice Bland too much, which is never a bad thing for defensive backs because it means they’re not getting picked on. Bland said Wednesday that his reps would be limited as he gets back into playing shape, but made the most of the work he saw on Thursday. – (Tommy Yarrish) Cowboys’ Dak Prescott not shying away from setting lofty goals – Todd Archer, ESPN.com Dak Prescott has his eyes set on the Super Bowl in 2026. Is he right for doing so? Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott isn’t afraid to let everybody know he carries big goals into 2026. Prescott wore a vintage T-shirt from the Cowboys’ last Super Bowl appearance — Super Bowl XXX in 1995 — when the team arrived in Oxnard, California, for training camp Monday. And while working out with skill players in Park City, Utah, before camp, Prescott came up with the anacronym GOTI, which stands for Greatest Offense There Is. “We want stuff in life a lot of times, but then when people start talking about it, you kind of hesitate. ‘Should I say that if they’re going to hold me to it?'” Prescott said. “Well, absolutely. Playing in this organization, being in it 10 years, going into year 11, I’m not going to shy away from it. When you don’t have it, it sucks when you don’t get to play for it. When you’re watching other teams play in the playoffs, there’s nothing worse than that. And so, yeah, I said I’d be the quarterback for the Dallas Cowboys when I was 6 years old and said I’d be in the NFL, and I got here. “A lot of things in my life, I said I’d do and I did it. And so why shy away from that now? Why shy away from asking people to hold me to the same standard that I believe that I can accomplish and this team can accomplish?” Jaishawn Barham & 6 Surprise Dallas Cowboys Turning Heads Early at Training Camp – Josh Sanchez, SI.com A look at a few surprises early in training camp. Jaishawn Barham, Linebacker Not enough great things can be said about third-rouond pick Jaishawn Barham. The former Michigan Wolverines star is a no-nonsense player whose physicality is jumping off of the screen, even without the team in pads. He has also shown an incredible attention to detail. If Barham is not going through drills himself, he is getting up close and personal, paying attention to every word the coaches say. Fans, media members, and even Brian Schottenheimer can’t help but turn their heads when Barham is taking reps. CB DaRon Bland, Shavon Revel ‘feeling good’ at start of training camp – Brian Martin, Blogging the Boys All eyes are on the cornerback room in the first week of training camp. The Dallas Cowboys spent the entire offseason attempting to upgrade the roster from top to bottom, and by most accounts they’ve succeeded. There are a few positions that may still need to be addressed at some point, but maybe cornerback will not be one. Dating back to December when DaRon Bland was placed on injured reserve, there’s been some concerns about his long-term future in Dallas. This is due to the injuries he sustained to his left foot that has required offseason surgery in consecutive years. No one quite knew how he would bounce back from surgery No. 2, but early reports definitely sound encouraging. Seeing that No. 26 is the Cowboys most seasoned and proven CB on the entire roster, and someone who is expected to start, him already “feeling really good” right now and running with the first-team defense is amazing news. Now, he just needs to find a way to remain healthy and return to his 2023 form. After two rather disappointing seasons, it’s easy to forget how well Bland played back in 2023. He was an All-Pro and set the NFL record for pick-sixes in a season with five, plus led the league in total interceptions with nine. That production ultimately led to the four-year, $92 million contract he signed in 2025. Daily discussion question: Who is standing out to you so far from camp?

title: J.K. Dobbins makes a pinky promise Broncos fans will love
summary: Whoever is reading this needs to stop right now and knock on wood. Now that we’ve got that out of the way, it’s no secret that J.K. Dobbins will play a crucial role in the success of the offense and the Denver Broncos this season. Specifically, his health and staying on the field. We don’t […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 5: J.K. Dobbins #27 of the Denver Broncos smiles against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on October 5, 2025 in Philadelphia, United States. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Whoever is reading this needs to stop right now and knock on wood. Now that we’ve got that out of the way, it’s no secret that J.K. Dobbins will play a crucial role in the success of the offense and the Denver Broncos this season. Specifically, his health and staying on the field. We don’t need to revisit it, since it’s well known at this point. Most recently, Dobbins had the fluke Lisfranc injury that ended his season and kept him out of the playoff run. Had he been available for the AFC Championship Game, who knows how that would have changed the outcome? This year, the Dobbins injury curse ends. After the first day of Broncos training camp, the Denver running back made a promise. #Broncos RB J.K. Dobbins makes his claim far and wide that he will be the “number one” rushing RB in the NFL in 2026. “I’m gonna be number one, and I’m gonna keep it there for the whole year. 17 games.” “This year, there won’t be any (injuries).” pic.twitter.com/K60ZsTvAxa — Luca Evans (@bylucaevans) July 31, 2026 “I know a lot of people will always say, ‘Oh, he’s good for the first 10 weeks,’” Dobbins said to the media on Friday. “I’ll be in the top three the first 10 weeks, right? ‘Dude, he does this every time.’ Well, this year, forget the top three. I keep saying it, and people will think I’m crazy, but I’m going to be No. 1. And I’m going to keep it there for the whole year. Seventeen games. “A lot of people will always get mad when I say, yeah, the injuries are over because I said it last year. That one was pretty fluky. This year, there won’t be any (injuries). There won’t be anything for anyone to say about my injuries because I’m going to play all 17 games, and I’m going to give my team everything I’ve got for all 17 games. And I will be there for all 17 games. I’ll pinky promise all of you right now about that.” If Dobbins is able to make good on his promise, the Broncos will win a lot of games in 2026. Prior to his injury against the Las Vegas Raiders, Dobbins was one of the best running backs in the NFL. And as he said, this seems to always happen. So what has Dobbins done to end his run of bad injury luck? “When I was younger, I could do the splits,” Dobbins said to the media. “I think I lost a little bit of that flexibility; I just wasn’t paying attention to it as much. Now I’m back to that. And back to my college weight. And I’m doing all the little things that’s going to, even if it’s some fluky stuff about to happen, I’m going to be like Elastiboy or Elastigirl. I’ll be over bouncing back up from it. Like, if I get hip-drop tackled, I’ll be like, I can touch my head with the back of my foot. And get back up.” J.K. Dobbins pinky promised the media he won’t get hurt this year. He double pinky promised the Broncos that. “Remember this day” — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) July 31, 2026 What you have to admire about Dobbins is his positive attitude. No matter what, he’ll just keep going. “I just can’t stop. I can’t lose. It’s just … I don’t want to let myself down either,” Dobbins said. “I’ve had the three big injuries, the knee first, which took like a couple of surgeries to clean up and get back to myself, I had the Achilles, and then I had the foot last year. I never really cared about it because I’m going to come back, and I’m going to be better. I’m going to keep doing it. Whatever life throws at you, you can’t give up, right? It’s a thing that I learned for the long haul, not just football. You get knocked down. Just keep getting back up.” Dobbins’ attitude and what he brings to the offense explain why the Broncos brought him back this offseason. As head coach Sean Payton said to the media on Thursday: “There’s a lot to him, and when you’re evaluating the type of injury he had, how it happened, and what he brings to the team, we had strong opinions (General Manager) George (Paton) and I, and the rest of the group about re-signing him. He was a big part of why we won 14 games last year, and sometimes that can get lost in the narrative. Certainly, he’s been injured, and yet what we were able to do when he was healthy had a lot to do with where we ended up, so it was unfortunate. I believe in the player a lot. That room has gotten markedly better from what I remember in 2023.” Plus, Dobbins believes this was always in the cards. “This organization is amazing,” Dobbins said. “I was born to be a Bronco. I know I was drafted to the Ravens and played for the Chargers for one year, but I think I’m truly a Bronco. All roads led to here. I said last year I had to get over the mountain to get here. And I’m here. And I’m here to stay. Now it’s a matter of Dobbins finally staying on the field. “I talked to somebody who said things come in threes,” Dobbins said to the media. “All on my left leg, I’ve had the knee, the Achilles, and the foot. It’s over. Whoever has my doll, on the left side, they’re done. Like, it’s just done. You’ll see.” It can’t hurt to knock on some wood again.

title: 2026 Denver Broncos Training Camp: Day 1 News and Notes
summary: Day 1 of Broncos Camp is FINALLY here! The Denver Broncos hit the practice field today for the official start of Broncos Camp. The fans were in attendance and made their presence known on Day 1, and the offense gave them a show. Nix and the rest of the Broncos quarterbacks came out firing and […]
full_text: ENGLEWOOD, CO - JULY 31: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos throws a pass during training camp at Broncos Park Powered by CommonSpirit on July 31, 2026 in Englewood, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Getty Images) | Getty Images Day 1 of Broncos Camp is FINALLY here! The Denver Broncos hit the practice field today for the official start of Broncos Camp. The fans were in attendance and made their presence known on Day 1, and the offense gave them a show. Nix and the rest of the Broncos quarterbacks came out firing and had multiple deep completions today. Is this a sign of things to come in Davis Webb’s offense? The defense didn’t go down quietly, though. Pat Surtain II did Pat Surtain II things, Riley Moss had a few PBUs, and Karene Reid had a forced fumble that could have gone for a touchdown. It was a solid first day from Broncos Camp. The work is underway 💪 pic.twitter.com/kZnJ2h53pD — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) July 31, 2026 In today’s piece, we have more on the Broncos’ hot start on offense, Bo Nix looking sharp, Jaylen Waddle looking smooth and unguardable, Evan Engram standing out, news and notes, injury updates, notable quotes, and more Offense starts camp HOT In the past decade or so, the Denver Broncos offense would typically start camp slowly. We would hear “the defense has an edge early” or that “it’s early,” and it would take a week or so before the offense would “win” a practice. That’s not the case this year. They looked good in their first acclimation practice on Wednesday, according to reports, and today showed off how explosive this offense can be. It all started early on with quarterback Bo Nix. He looked sharp, according to reports, and did not look like a quarterback who missed the vast majority of the offseason practices. He started the day with multiple chunk plays in 7-on-7s and continued that into the team period. When team drills started, his first completion was to Jaylen Waddle on a slant route. Something we will likely see a lot of this upcoming season. Bo Nix with a DEEP 50-yard completion to Marvin Mims. Great throw. Great catch. Riley Moss in good coverage. — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) July 31, 2026 However, Nix wasn’t the only quarterback looking good today. During team drills, backup quarterback Jarrett Stidham made the early “play of camp” when he hit veteran tight end Evan Engram for a 50+ yard touchdown (More on Engram later). Third-string quarterback Sam Ehlinger shined some today as well when he hit Hakeem Butler for a touchdown. Then came the Marvin Mims portion of practice. First, he caught a 35-yard gain from Jarrett Stidham, and then he had the biggest play of the day and camp thus far. He hauled in a 50+ yard bomb from Bo Nix with Riley Moss in coverage for a touchdown. He also had two catches in the final move-the-ball period. Head Coach Sean Payton was asked if they hope to open up the passing game with more explosive pass plays. He said they are always trying to stretch the field and added that Bo Nix is really good at getting the ball deep, and players like Marvin Mims Jr. have been a consistent down the field deep threat for them. “I think we’re always trying to stretch the field. I think that it’s something that [QB] Bo [Nix] has been really good at with his arm strength. [WR] Marvin [Mims Jr.] has been very consistent. If you just looked about when we’ve called on him for those opportunities, he’s come down with a lot of plays. To answer your question, I think there’s always that mindset within the framework of a game. What are our explosives? Then when we watch the tape, some of those are coming off of scrambles, some of them realistically are going to be getting up… Some might be the defense laying off a sack, so you just have to look at the tape, but it was good to see the ball get down the field.” The defense did have its moments, including winning the final team drill, but the offense was the overall winner of the day. They made a lot of big explosive plays and looked sharp and in control early on in camp, which is new. Overall, Bo Nix, Jaylen Waddle, Marvin Mims, and Evan Engram were the standout players on the offensive side of the ball. Good news overall, and hopefully it is a thing that continues throughout the remainder of training camp. Engram has a big Day 1 One of the biggest question marks surrounding the team is their tight end production. Evan Engram was a big addition last season and was a standout player during camp/preseason, but didn’t live up to expectations during the season. However, on Day 1 of Broncos Camp, Engram was once again a standout player. Today, Engram was arguably the Broncos’ best pass catcher and could be on the verge of flourishing under offensive coordinator Davis Webb. Keep in mind, Engram and Webb have a close personal relationship and were former teammates with the Giants, so Webb may unlock Engram’s potential in this offense. Evan Engram is having a DAY: Been targeted multiple times with multiple catches during team, including the 50-yard bomb from Jarrett Stidham. The Davis Webb play caller seems to be benefitting him a ton. — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) July 31, 2026 He was heavily targeted during today’s practice and had a long 50+ yard reception from backup quarterback Jarrett Stidham. So, it was a solid first day of Broncos Camp for the veteran Evan Engram, and hopefully, something that continues throughout the summer. After practice, head coach Sean Payton was asked about Engram, and he told reporters that he believes he can “definitely be a big asset for us” and that one of his strengths is that he can run. “I think he can definitely be a big asset for us. I think one of his strengths is he can run, and I think it’s good that he’s getting these reps along with the younger guys.” Engram showed off that strength today with that 50+ yard completion, and hopefully we see more of that running ability this upcoming season. Payton was also asked about the Davis Webb factor when it comes to Engram and if he has any new ideas on how to use the veteran tight end. He told reporters “yes to some degree” but added it’s about executing and that the ball is going to be spread around and those touches need to be earned. “I would say yes to some degree. I think he’s trying to find different ways where he might have a matchup, and I think that’s a good thing. Now it’s just executing, and it’s ball security, catching, the landmarks, some of the nuances. He’s one other piece where you’re trying to spread the ball around. Who’s going to earn those touches? Those have to be earned.” The Broncos do have a lot of mouths to feed on the offensive side of the ball. They have three backs who can all contribute on the ground and as pass catchers, five wide receivers including Jaylen Waddle who will likely get a heavy workload, and multiple tight ends including Engram and rookie Justin Joly. So, like all the other players, Engram will need to earn these targets, and hopefully, he can continue to do that as we progress throughout the summer and into the regular season. JK Dobbins promises that he won’t get hurt this season One of the big question marks surrounding this team heading into the season is the health of veteran running back JK Dobbins. He has dealt with injuries throughout his career, including multiple significant lower body injuries and unfortunately suffered a season-ending Lisfranc injury last season while with the Broncos. Now, in his second season with the team, Dobbins is vowing to stay healthy. J.K. Dobbins pinky promised the media he won't get hurt this year 😳 "Remember this day" pic.twitter.com/4DezK5PVPV — DNVR Broncos (@DNVR_Broncos) July 31, 2026 Dobbins told reporters he pinky promised the team that they won’t regret bringing him back and that he will be out there for them. He then joked with the media that he would buy them a drink if he does indeed get hurt and told them to remember this day. He also added that he’s going to lead the NFL in rushing and be…

title: Details behind Broncos guard Ben Powers restructured contract
summary: Last week, it was reported that starting left guard Ben Powers accepted a pay cut from the Denver Broncos. 9NEWS Denver’s Mike Klis reported that Powers accepted a restructured one-year deal that will leave him with less pay but a higher guarantee. full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - JANUARY 17: Ben Powers #74 of the Denver Broncos looks on from the field during an NFL divisional playoff football game against the Buffalo Bills at Empower Field at Mile High on January 17, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. The new deal frees up $7.5M of 2026 cap space for Denver. https://t.co/qsG2PU5fy3 — Spotrac (@spotrac) July 31, 2026 This extra cap space is beneficial for the Broncos because they have a few pending free agents they may want to lock up. The team also drafted former Boise State left tackle Kage Casey in the fourth round of the 2026 NFL Draft. He is shifting inside for the Broncos and is expected to focus on the left guard position. Rookies can be plug-and-play players along the offensive line, so he could be someone to watch for that job as well. title: Talanoa Hufanga and Broncos defense focused on improving in 2026
summary: Over the past two seasons, the Denver Broncos defense has been a forced to be reckoned with. Their penchant for sacks has been their forte. Without question, their ability to get after opposing quarterbacks is second to none. They have done well limiting big plays down the field and tout one of the top performing […]
full_text: CENTENNIAL , CO - JUNE 4: Talanoa Hufanga (9) of the Denver Broncos talks to members of the media during OTAs at the Broncos Park in Centennial, Colorado on Thursday, June 4, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images Over the past two seasons, the Denver Broncos defense has been a forced to be reckoned with. Their penchant for sacks has been their forte. Without question, their ability to get after opposing quarterbacks is second to none. They have done well limiting big plays down the field and tout one of the top performing third down units in all of football. Even so, the defense remains hungry. This year, the coaches and players are looking to build upon ‘the standard’ they have set for themselves in recent seasons. Yesterday, after the team’s second ramp-up practice of training camp, safety Talanoa Hufanga took time to field questions on how the Broncos’ defense can make strides and be even better in 2026. “What does that standard look like? It’s guys being in early, it’s guys staying late, it’s guys studying and it’s guys learning. At the end of the day, it’s really the type of style that you play. The schematics is always going to be down there and that’s game plan to game plan, but what’s the style that you want,” stated Hufanga. Hufanga, one of the highlight free agent signings from last season, took quickly to Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph’s scheme. He was an impact player on the squad in his first season donning orange and blue. The stalwart safety started every game for the Broncos and amassed 106 tackles, 2 sacks, 11 passes defended, and one forced fumble. That top-tier play and production earned him second-team All-Pro honors. His knack for bone-crushing hits, ability to cover well, and make plays against the run was a terrific addition to the backend of the Broncos’ defense. Entering his second season with the franchise, he feels a lot more comfortable with the playbook and what Joseph wants to call throughout the course of the game. Such knowledge should bode well for his gridiron endeavors in ’26. However, he and his teammates know they can raise ‘the standard’ even higher this season. That means performing better in one key category—turnovers—which was the major point of emphasis for them at the advent of training camp and earlier in the offseason. “For sure, it was the first thing. For us, it’s just really attacking the ball. Whether it’s in the air or in the ground game. For everybody, it was really just a lack of turnovers,” stated Hufanga. “We did a really good job of getting sacks, but how can we get to sacks with a force fumble? Or how can we change this pass deflection into an interception or a tip just to get somebody else an interception? It’s been talked about and it’s been drilled.” Last season, Denver’s defense was tied for the fourth least turnovers in the league with just 14 during the regular season. That’s nineteen turnovers shy of the Chicago Bears who led the NFL in that category in 2025, and about seven turnovers below league average. Below average won’t cut it for this year’s Broncos. That certainly doesn’t meet ‘the standard’. In order to forge themselves into true Super Bowl contenders, fighting and clawing their way from the bottom of that list towards the top will be mission critical. Just one big turnover can change the momentum and course of the game. The Broncos did well in one-score battles last season. Nevertheless, finding a way to create more turnovers through the course of the upcoming season will help turn some of those close games into decisive victories. “I really messed up last year when it came to those things. I left a lot of—we call it money—but money on the field as a team. For me, I’m going in and working and hopefully coming down with a few this year.”

title: Denver Broncos roster review: Offensive lineman Matt Peart
summary: The offensive line is a premier strength of the Denver Broncos. They tout a quality starting lineup and good depth behind them with promising young players. Under the guidance of Head Coach Sean Payton and Assistant Head Coach Zach Strief, the Broncos’ offensive trenches have once again become a formidable force for the franchise. One […]
full_text: Nov 10, 2024; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Denver Broncos offensive tackle Matt Peart (79) at the line of scrimmage against the Kansas City Chiefs during the game at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images | Denny Medley-Imagn Images The offensive line is a premier strength of the Denver Broncos. They tout a quality starting lineup and good depth behind them with promising young players. Under the guidance of Head Coach Sean Payton and Assistant Head Coach Zach Strief, the Broncos’ offensive trenches have once again become a formidable force for the franchise. One player vying to make the final 53-man roster this year is Matt Peart. The Broncos signed Peart to a two-year deal worth $7 million during the 2024 free agency period. In his first season with the Broncos, Peart was a valuable swing man in the offensive trenches. He appeared in every game and started two of them. Last season, he made the final roster and appeared in six games with one start before a knee injury ended his season in mid-October. Entering the final year of his deal, Peart appears to be on the outside looking in with respect to making the Broncos’ final roster. Let’s discuss the odds of him earning one of the backup spots on the team. Player Profile Age: 29 | Experience: Seventh Year | College: Uconn | Height: 6’7” | Weight: 318 pounds 2025 Statistics : Appeared in six games with one start replacing Ben Powers at left guard. Missed remainder of season after suffering a knee injury early in October. Matt Peart’s 2026 outlook with the Broncos Last season, the Broncos kept nine offensive linemen on their active roster. Peart was one of four backups alongside Alex Palczeswki, Frank Crum and Alex Forsyth. I expect the Broncos to carry the same number at the position this season. However, I’m not too sure Peart will be one of them. Denver drafted Boise State offensive lineman Kage Casey in the fourth round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Given such, that is one less reserve spot available or up for grabs compared to ’25. Barring some sort of unforeseen circumstance, Casey seems like an absolute lock to make the final 53-man roster. Additionally, the Broncos rewarded Palczewski with a two-year contract this offseason. They clearly believe in his potential and believe his continued development will be crucial for the state of Denver’s offensive line moving forward. Last but not least, I presume the Broncos’ brass would like to see Crum continue to grow. He appeared in just one game during the ‘24 season but was active for 11 last season and showed some promise in his limited snap share on offense. Final Thoughts Peart is one of the veteran players who made last year’s final roster that I expect to be cut in this year’s roster trimming process. Truth be told, I’m not worried about his skill or talent level. He has over 1,000 career offensive snaps as a pinch starter—a lot more than most any backup Denver is poised to bring back. However, coming off injury and facing stiff competition from several other young players the team is trying to develop will make it a tough challenge for him. Peart will have to stay healthy, compete at a high-level during training camp, and perform well during the preseason to make the squad.
