Sportswire) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye described his wide receiver room by two words on Friday: crowded and competitive. The Patriots roster currently features seven wide receivers with NFL experience, as they acquired A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs this offseason to work with Kayshon Boutte, DeMario Douglas, Mack Hollins, Kyle Williams, and Efton Chism III. As the roster must eventually dwindle down to 53 players, keeping all seven feels far fetched. That means at least one will be the odd man out. Among the group, Patriots fans view one as the clear odd man out. In the results of the latest SB Nation Reacts survey, 43% of participants said that was Efton Chism III . The comment section, however, was more split: Mosi_Tatupu Probably Chism gets cut but can’t rule out an aging Hollins or a trade for Boutte or injury, but as of right now it’s Chism on the bubble. Chu I put Chism because he may make it to PS and I think he redundant to Pop who I think is better underneath quick slot. Imagine McDaniels coming up with a wr version of Lil Woodhead. NittanyLions2.0: Boutte. I think he gets traded with his value increasing with his play. Hopefully he shows it in pre season. Might be able to get a fourth for him. 7i165 Hollins as he is in last year of his contract and could free 4m cap space. But only if other players show they are able to be as effective as him zionlion02 I’ll go wild card and say Demario. I think his play is too chaotic and uncontrolled and I’ve seen numerous mentions of him not being able to run routes. Boutte is a far better receiver playing a harder to replace role. mathblaster97 Cut Chism and stash him on the PS All in all, this week’s survey results look as follows: 21% of voters would prefer to keep all seven, with multiple participants noting the depth would be welcomed for injury insurance. DeMario Douglas, who enters the final year of his rookie contract, was the next receiver to be listed receiving 15% of the votes. Despite potentially being the most likely to be the odd man out after a trade request this past spring entering the last year of his contract, Kayshon Boutte received the least amount of votes at 4%. No matter who is on the outside-looking-in come Week 1, New England is hoping the improvements atop the wide receiver depth chart will help them get back to the Super Bowl and finish the job this time, as they currently have the eighth highest odds on FanDuel Sportsbook to win Super Bowl LXI — the fifth highest odds in the AFC.

title: What releasing Otis Reese means for the Patriots
summary: Before entering the practice fields for their sixth session of this year’s training camp, the New England Patriots decided to part ways with a member of their linebacker group. Otis Reese, who had originally joined the team via its practice squad last November, was released. With no follow-up move happening yet, let’s analyze what we […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - AUGUST 9: Otis Reese IV #41 of the Tennessee Titans walks onto the field prior to an NFL preseason football game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium on August 9, 2025 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Before entering the practice fields for their sixth session of this year’s training camp, the New England Patriots decided to part ways with a member of their linebacker group . Otis Reese, who had originally joined the team via its practice squad last November, was released. With no follow-up move happening yet, let’s analyze what we know about this particular transactions and what it means for the Patriots. Not a major move When we wrote his Patriots scouting report , this is what we had to say about Reese under the “How safe is his roster spot?” section: A former practice squad player on a minimum deal who hasn’t played in any NFL game in almost 19 months? That is textbook roster bubble. Reese will get a chance to compete for a backup spot behind starting linebackers Robert Spillane and Christian Elliss, but he needs to step up his game in order to make it onto the 53-man team. The Patriots won’t hesitate cutting him if he does not. As this one paragraph already outlined earlier this month, his release even before the start of preseason should not come as a surprise. Reese was a depth and special teams player only, who was facing long odds to begin with. Apparently, the team agreed and decided to make a move sooner rather than later. Open roster spot The biggest consequence of the Patriots releasing Reese is that it opens a spot on the team’s roster. Including roster-exempt offensive tackle Lorenz Metz, 90 of the 91 available spots are currently filled. While the team will have to trim down to 53 within the next month, Reese’s former spot remaining unoccupied is unlikely to happen. The question is how New England wants to fill it. On Friday, two players — safeties Eric Butler and Tysheem Johnson — were in town for free agency workouts . Neither was signed, but this is one possible avenue the team could explore. Decreased linebacker depth The Patriots entered Friday with nine linebackers on the roster. They exit it with the following eight in the fold : Linebacker (8): Robert Spillane (14), Christian Elliss (53), K.J. Britt (35), Chad Muma (49), Amari Gainer (99), Namdi Obiazor (48), Khalil Jacobs (59), Riley Wilson (51) As mentioned in the excerpt above, Robert Spillane and Christian Elliss are the starters at the linebacker position. Based on the first six practices of camp, K.J. Britt and Chad Muma are the next men up, even though undrafted rookie Khalil Jacobs has had some solid moments as of late. No cap impact Reese was among a group of veterans playing on a non-guaranteed $1.075 million base salary. This is why his release has no impact on the Patriots’ salary cap: removing him from the books means that another player on the same salary and cap hit is taking his place on the Top 51 list. According to Miguel Benzan, New England finds itself $33.7 million under the cap at the moment. This places them in the top eight in the NFL at the moment.

full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, IN - DECEMBER 07: Oregon Ducks DB Tysheem Johnson (0) celebrates a tackle during the Big Ten Championship football game between the Penn State Nittany Lions and the Oregon Ducks on December 7, 2024 at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, IN (Photo by James Black/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After one roster spot opened, two free agents visited Gillette Stadium. The San Diego State product appeared in 48 games, including 23 starts, during his Aztecs career. Blocking a pair of punts, Butler had a hand in 119 tackles, one sack, one forced fumble, one fumble recovery and one interception returned a touchdown. Johnson, listed at 5-foot-10, 195 pounds, made collegiate stops at Ole Miss and Oregon before going undrafted in 2025. The 23-year-old defensive back appeared in 53 games, including 46 starts, while totaling 131 tackles, two sacks and six interceptions. Waived by the Chicago Bears with an injury designation at the 53-man roster deadline last summer, Johnson finished his rookie season on the practice squad of the Atlanta Falcons. He was waived in May. On Friday morning, the Patriots waived linebacker Otis Reese, who finished 2025 as a member of the practice squad. The organization currently carries an active roster of 90, yet an exemption for German offensive tackle Lorenz Metz through the NFL’s International Player Pathway. The seventh session of training camp in Foxborough is set for 10:15 a.m. ET on Saturday.

title: 6 performances of note from the Patriots’ sixth training camp practice
summary: For a second straight day, the New England Patriots put on their full pads on Friday. This meant that, for a second straight day, the intensity was high in Foxborough. To recap the sixth practice of the summer, please make sure to head over to our Patriots training camp notebook. In the meantime, here is […]
full_text: Jul 28, 2026; Foxborough, MA, USA; New England Patriots wide receiver Cameron Dorner (88) and safety Peter Manuma (34) do a drill during training camp at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect For a second straight day, the New England Patriots put on their full pads on Friday. This meant that, for a second straight day, the intensity was high in Foxborough. To recap the sixth practice of the summer, please make sure to head over to our Patriots training camp notebook . In the meantime, here is who caught our eye during the session. Standout of the day QB Drake Maye: The Patriots’ starting quarterback was close to perfect on Friday, stacking a second straight strong practice. Maye completed 19 of 21 combined pass attempts in 7-on-7s and 11-on-11s, with his lone incompletions being by choice: he took one throwaway in 7s and another in 11s, even though the latter was seemingly picked off by Christian Gonzalez for the interception. Still, Maye impressed. Not only is he spreading the ball around well, he also is making multiple highlight-reel throws each day. On Friday, a 7-on-7 touchdown to Romeo Doubs over Gonzalez’s outstretched arms was a highlight, as was a deep touchdown to A.J. Brown. The connection with those two is developing nicely, and so is the Patriots’ passing offense as a whole. Ultimately, it all goes back to No. 10. Other performances of note WR Romeo Doubs: After A.J. Brown had his best of camp on Thursday, the other high-profile offseason addition at wide receiver followed suit on Friday. Doubs had his best practice of the summer, having successful reps in 1-on-1s, 2-on-2s and 7-on-7s — the latter including a contested touchdown versus Christian Gonzalez. He was not targeted in 11-on-11s, but it still felt like big step in the right direction. WR Cameron Dorner: The Patriots’ undrafted rookie receivers are unlikely to compete for roster spots; there simply is too much talent ahead of them on the depth chart. They are in a fight for the practice squad, however, and Dorner seems to have started separating himself from the bunch. He had another good practice on Friday and has built a good rapport with third-string quarterback Behren Morton. OT Caleb Lomu: With Morgan Moses limited, the Patriots’ rookie tackle saw increased action on Friday. He responded with an up-and-down performance. While Lomu did look solid during team drills, he had a rough 1-on-1 blocking period. Most of the media tent had him going 0-4 in his matchups with losses to Bradyn Swinson twice and once each against Elijah Ponder and Amari Gainer. He seemed to particularly struggle with speed. OL Mehki Butler and OL Caedan Wallace: It looks like the second-string offense has a new member. After the former third-round pick Wallace served as both a backup left and right guard during the spring and early training camp, sophomore Mehki Butler filled that role on Friday. That is a nice promotion for Butler, while the end of the road might be nearing for Wallace. The Patriots will hold their seventh practice of training camp on Saturday. Gates are scheduled to open at 9:15 p.m. ET for that session, with practice again set to start approximately an hour later.

title: Drake Maye and A.J. Brown finding their rhythm at Patriots camp
summary: Building chemistry can take time. Drake Maye and A.J. Brown learned that over the Patriots’ four training camp practices, as the duo struggled to get on the same page. But since the pads came on Thursday, their connection has come to life. “Just giving more chances to him,” Maye said. “I think you see with […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - JULY 27: Drake Maye #10 of the New England Patriots spots A.J. Brown #1 of the New England Patriots during New England Patriots Training Camp on July 27, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Fred Kfoury III/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Building chemistry can take time. Drake Maye and A.J. Brown learned that over the Patriots’ four training camp practices, as the duo struggled to get on the same page. But since the pads came on Thursday, their connection has come to life. “Just giving more chances to him,” Maye said. “I think you see with the ball in his hands what he can do, so just finding more chances, intermediate, short, deep, just not shying away from it – I am not going to shy away from him. That is how I play. I am going to keep going at it, and it could be the fifth play in a row I am going to give him the rock.” On Thursday in high red-zone work, Maye connected on four of his five passes to Brown, resulting in at least two would-be touchdowns on slants. Still waiting to see the duo strike a big play in full-field work, they delivered quickly on Friday. Maye’s first pass of the day in full-team work was a deep shot down the right sideline that Brown hauled in for a gain of more than 40 yards after beating Christian Gonzalez on a double move. The quarterback later found Brown on back-to-back completions in low red-zone 11-on-11 work. “You feel like you know when things are clicking. I feel like we had some good plays today,” Maye said. “He’s a force in this league, he’s been a force in this league… I am blessed to play with a player like him and looking forward to giving him the rock and seeing him do his thing.” The recent success has stemmed from more opportunities, but also from the relationship the two have built off the field since Brown arrived in a trade on June 1. “It is great for us to talk and pull up some old things that he has run and how he liked to run them and what he liked to do, and the routes for his different looks,” Maye said. “So, it is just trying to feel the connectivity building now. I think that is the biggest thing with a player like him and a lot of players that we have. It is my job to try to get him the ball when they want and when they, when I feel like they are open, and that is what he’s trying to build a relationship with me and him. I think you’re just seeing it get better every day.” Maye’s success has extended well beyond Brown, as the quarterback has rarely seen the ball hit the ground over the first two padded practices. On Friday, he found Hunter Henry, DeMario Douglas and Mack Hollins for touchdowns while also connecting with Eli Raridon, Romeo Doubs and Kayshon Boutte down the field. “I think you find that during training camp. You try to find a rhythm,” Maye said. “I feel like being accurate is one of the number one things of playing quarterback and putting the ball in the right spot and giving our guys chances, and that is what I’m doing and our guys are making plays.”

title: Patriots training camp recap: Drake Maye stacks another strong practice
summary: Following their first padded practice of training camp, the New England Patriots were back to work on Friday and once again donned full pads as the focus was mainly in the red zone again. Here’s what went down on the practice fields behind Gillette Stadium. Attendance Absent: CB Carlton Davis III, DT Christian Barmore (new) […]
full_text: Jul 28, 2026; Foxborough, MA, USA; New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye (10) throws a pass during training camp at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Following their first padded practice of training camp, the New England Patriots were back to work on Friday and once again donned full pads as the focus was mainly in the red zone again. Here’s what went down on the practice fields behind Gillette Stadium. Attendance Absent: CB Carlton Davis III, DT Christian Barmore (new) Returnee: CB Brandon Crossley Limited: OT Morgan Moses, OG Alijah Vera-Tucker PUP/NFI: ED Gabe Jacas, RB Terrell Jennings, TE C.J. Dippre, ED Harold Landry III, S Brenden Schooler Injuries: N/A In the secondary, the Patriots saw Brandon Crossley return after missing yesterday’s practice while Carlton Davis remained sidelined. Christian Barmore was then a new absence, while veteran offensive lineman Morgan Moses and Alijah Vera-Tucker were limited for likely veteran rest. Takeaways Maye’s day: It was another strong showing for Drake Maye as the quarterback continues to stack positive days together. After throwing touchdowns to Eli Raridon and Romeo Doubs to open practice in 7-on-7, Maye was efficient and decisive as work remained in the low red zone as he tossed just one incompletion. In addition to a pair of short completions to A.J. Brown, Maye threw touchdowns to Hunter Henry, Mack Hollins, and DeMario Douglas — the last coming with the QB dropping a ball in the bucket in the back left corner of the end zone. In total, he completed 19 of 21 combined passes in 7-on-7s and 11-on-11s. His only two incompletions were throwaways, with one of them seemingly ending up a Christian Gonzalez interception. Dialing up the pressure: While Maye was sharp throughout the day, it came with some pressure around him. After New England’s front held up in pass protection on Day 1 in pads, the defensive got home on Friday. That came from several blitzes to produce free rushers, with Craig Woodson and Kevin Byard in the backfield at times. New England’s offensive line, which was without Morgan Moses and Alijah Vera-Tucker at times, also struggled to find much room in the ground game for the second straight padded practice. Big play A.J.: The Drake Maye-A.J. Brown connection came to life in the red zone on Thursday, but the duo was still in search of a big play in full-field work. It didn’t take long on Friday as Maye’s first pass of the day in 11-on-11 was a 40-plus yard completion down the left sideline to Brown, who got open on a double move against Christian Gonzalez as the corner guarded the sticks with New England blitzing. Brown then hauled in two short touchdown completions in low red zone work from Maye as the chemistry and physicality continue to show in that area of the field. As for the rest of New England’s wideouts, Romeo Doubs went up-and-over Gonzalez for a strong touchdown catch in 7s, but did not see a target in full team work. ROMEO OH ROMEO 😯 pic.twitter.com/43jPCTfeHr — New England Patriots (@Patriots) July 31, 2026 DeMario Douglas was more active today, while Kyle Williams ended the day hauling in a goal line fade from Behren Morton and also made a strong contested sideline catch from Tommy DeVito. Efton Chism III shined in an early 2-on-2 goal line period, where was a tough cover for any New England defensive back and continues to be sprinkled in with the top offense in run looks. UDFA Cameron Dorner also stacked a second straight strong day together with three catches from Morton. Kick returners: The Patriots repped more of a live kick return drill for the first time this offseason in front of reporters, which gave a look at the kick returner depth chart. That was led off by Kyle Williams and Lan Larison, while Efton Chism, Kobe Prentice, Jam Miller, Myles Montgomery and Cameron Dorner also saw reps. Williams had a strong return to open the period with Larison as the up blocker, while Chism appeared to break the longest as the unit in front of him opened a wide cutback lane. Other notes: Another strong day from rookie tight end Eli Raridon, who caught three passes (one from Maye) in 7s and a sail route in full team work on an impressive throw from Tommy DeVito. Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson continued to make plays in the passing game against New England’s linebacker. Rookie running back Jam Miller also caught the eye again finding running lanes. Caleb Lomu settled in at right tackle in full team work, but the rookie had a rough start in 1-on-1s — including losses to Elijah Ponder and Bradyn Swinson, who won with a strong swim move. Will Campbell held up well again in 1-on-1s including a win over Dre’Mont Jones. Some movement on the backup offensive line with Mehki Butler replacing Caedan Wallace at guard. Ben Brown and Andrew Rupcich continue to serve as the top two depth options along the interior. Andy Borregales appeared to connect on five of his six field goal attempts continuing to work between roughly 30 and 50 yards. The Patriots will be back to work on Saturday where the current expectation is they will be back in full pads. Practice is set to begin at 10:15 a.m. ET and Mike Vrabel will speak beforehand.

summary: In this week’s Saints reacts poll, we asked our readers which quarterback do they think will win the backup position? An overwhelming 69% of voters said that it will be 3rd year QB Spencer Rattler. The 25-year-old who was drafted by the Saints in the 5th round of the 2024 NFL Draft, enters 2026 with a […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - OCTOBER 26: Spencer Rattler #2 of the New Orleans Saints warms up before a game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Caesars Superdome on October 26, 2025 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Sean Gardner/Getty Images) | Getty Images In this week’s Saints reacts poll, we asked our readers which quarterback do they think will win the backup position? An overwhelming 69% of voters said that it will be 3rd year QB Spencer Rattler. The 25-year-old who was drafted by the Saints in the 5th round of the 2024 NFL Draft, enters 2026 with a 1-13 record as a starter over the past two year. Last season, Rattler lost the starting job to then rookie 2nd-round pick Tyler Shough halfway through the Saints’ loss to the Buccaneers in Week 8. However, this is Rattler’s second full season under Kellen Moore and with that comes more knowledge and understanding of Moore’s offensive system, which obviously makes him the number one candidate to be the backup quarterback. However, you shouldn’t count out yet what Kellen Moore can do with Zach Wilson, who the Saints signed in free agency. Wilson was the 2nd overall pick in the 2021, who just never found his way with New York Jets and making stops in Denver and Miami the past two seasons. Moore is an offensive genius and a former quarterback himself, so if anyone can help Wilson develop into his full potential, it would be him. With Saints training camp now into the third day of practice, we are starting to get a better look at the QBs in both team and individual drills, so this is one off the radar battle to be watched. summary: Today was the third day of Saints training camp, and the offense found different ways to feature Travis Etienne Jr. throughout multiple team periods. full_text: Today was the third day of Saints training camp, and the offense found different ways to feature Travis Etienne Jr. throughout multiple team periods. The combination of Etienne and Alvin Kamara looks like exactly what Saints fans were hoping for when the team paired the dynamic running back duo this offseason. Etienne spoke with the media following practice, and during his session he highlighted how, even at this stage of his career, he is still able to learn from Kamara. He went on to say, “I’m watching him, trying to soak it all in and seeing what I can take from his game and incorporate into mine.” Running back is a position where only one player is typically on the field at a time. However, a good running back room can feed off the energy and relationships within the group, especially when the players have developed strong communication and trust that allow them to help each other even when they’re not in the game. Etienne Jr. was asked how running backs can build chemistry if they aren’t on the field together. CSC’s Tina Howell quoted him as saying, “As long as we’re winning, we don’t care. It’s a 17-game season, and we’re here for a reason. The main focus is on winning games, getting to the playoffs, and winning a championship. You don’t get there by being selfish.” #Saints RB Travis Etienne Jr. said he and Alvin Kamara are building off each other, and their chemistry is only going to get better. Their focus is on winning a game and not on the amount of carries they get. "As long as we're winning, we don't care. It's a 17-game season and… — Tina Howell (@TinaM_Howell) July 31, 2026 Etienne Jr. was also asked about his role alongside Kamara. Per NOF, he said they don’t care who takes the field first because they both know they can make plays, and they plan to feed off each other’s success. title: How Chris Olave’s Extension Stacks Up Against the 2022 NFL Draft’s Top Wide Receivers
summary: The New Orleans Saints finally locked in their WR1 under contract, giving him an extension that keeps him on the team until 2030. Olave’s deal is worth up to $132 million with $90 million in guarantees. With his extension, the 2022 first-round pick becomes the sixth highest-paid wide receiver in the NFL. Above him are […]
full_text: The New Orleans Saints finally locked in their WR1 under contract, giving him an extension that keeps him on the team until 2030. Olave’s deal is worth up to $132 million with $90 million in guarantees. With his extension, the 2022 first-round pick becomes the sixth highest-paid wide receiver in the NFL. Above him are Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Ja’Marr Chase, Drake London, Justin Jefferson, and CeeDee Lamb. Olave is also the final of the 2022 first-round wide receivers who are with the team that drafted them to receive a contract extension, so how does the former Buckeye’s new contract stack up against his draft class? WR Garrett Wilson, New York Jets New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson was the first of the wide receivers taken in the 2022 NFL Draft to sign an extension. Ahead of the 2025 NFL season, the Jets signed Wilson to a four-year $130 million deal. The Jets’ standout receiver has an average annual value of $32.5 million. When Wilson signed his contract, everyone in the Saints community paid attention. Wilson’s contract would be the blueprint for New Orleans when it was time to pay their star. Fittingly, the Saints signed Olave to a similar deal, with Olave squeaking out an extra $500,00 a year, earning $33 million annually. The former Buckeye teammates have had similar experiences in their young careers. Both were drafted to struggling franchises with questions at quarterback, yet each wideout has found success in the league. In his four seasons with New York, Wilson has accumulated 3,644 receiving yards and 18 touchdowns in 58 games. Olave, who has appeared in 55 games, just edges out Wilson with 3,728 receiving yards and 19 touchdowns. Length: 4 years Total Value: $130 million AAV: $32.5 million Guaranteed: $90 million WR Drake London, Atlanta Falcons Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Drake London was the first of the wideouts taken in the 2022 NFL Draft, and he is fittingly the highest-paid, getting a four-year $141 million contract earlier in the offseason. London’s deal came as a surprise. While the 6-foot-4 wideout has been solid in his early career, he’s only gone over 1,000 receiving yards once, achieving 1,271 yards in 2024. While the Falcons’ wideout has had the best single-season of his fellow 2022 draftees, he hasn’t been as consistent. London went for 919 yards and 7 touchdowns in 2025 before earning his contract. What London has been able to do that Olave and Wilson haven’t, however, is remain healthy. The former eighth overall pick appeared in 12+ games each season and has played in 16+ games in each of his first three years. In 62 games, London has logged 3,961 receiving yards and 22 touchdowns, both the most of any other 2022 wideouts. Length: 4 years Total Value: $141,054,000 AAV: $35,263,599 Guaranteed: $99,871,000 WR Jameson Williams, Detroit Lions The Detroit Lions followed quickly behind the Jets to extend their star wideout, signing Jameson Williams to a three-year $83 million deal with $67 million guaranteed just a month later. Similarly to Londo’s, Williams extension came as a surprise. The former Alabama wideout only achieved a single 1,000-yard season before signing his deal, logging just 395 yards total in his first two years. But the Lions didn’t go all in on Williams. While he earned a significant payday, 17 wide receivers earn more annually than the former first-round pick. With Amon-Ra St. Brown on the roster, Detroit only had to give Williams WR2 money rather than paying him as their first option. Williamson has become electric since signing his deal, however. Over his last two seasons, he’s logged back-to-back 1,000+ yard campaigns and scored 14 touchdowns in that span. Despite his productive last two seasons, the star wideout is behind his fellow draft class in receiving yards, logging 2,513 in four seasons. Length: 3 years Total Value: $80 million AAV: $26,666,667 Guaranteed: $66.58 million The 2022 NFL Draft class was wide receiver-heavy. While other first-round receivers such as Jahan Dotson and Treylon Burks couldn’t find as much success as their counterparts, the wide picks that landed were hits. Olave’s deal makes him the second-highest-paid wide receiver in his draft class, and he’s earned it. Through their first four seasons, Olave has the second-most receiving yards and touchdowns in that span. While health has remained a concern, a growing connection with second-year quarterback Tyler Shough means New Orleans had to lock their star receiver up on a significant contract.

full_text: On Saturday, August 1, 2026, New Orleans Saints wide receivers Chris Olave and Jordyn Tyson will host The Kickoff: Back‑to‑School Giveaway which will provide hundreds of local students with backpacks, school supplies, and access to essential community resources as they prepare for their upcoming school year. The event will be held at The City of Love, located on 8601 Palmetto Street in New Orleans from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. Presented by the Olave Family Foundation in partnership with The City of Love, The Kickoff is designed to equip students with the tools they need for academic success while strengthening connections between professional athletes, community organizations, and the families they serve. “Investing in young people extends far beyond the game,” said Chris Olave. “We want students to walk into the new school year feeling prepared and supported.” While attending the event is free, registration is required and each child must be registered individually using their name and they must also be present to receive a backpack and school supplies. Although the injury may be an annoyance, Smyth joked about how he is “the only player on the team who doesn’t need my hands.” The Irishman took over full-time kicking responsibilities for New Orleans in the last six games of 2025, during which he converted 12-16 FGA for 75% accuracy. Even with experience on the roster, the Saints brought in former UFL kicker Tanner Brown to compete for the starting gig and challenge Smyth to improve. Brown gained notoriety in the spring football league for his powerful leg, and New Orleans is hoping that could translate to the NFL, where distance is becoming an increasingly important X-factor for special teams. Even though Smyth’s injured thumb should not affect his leg swing, it’s certainly something to keep an eye on as this training camp battle trudges on. Smyth reportedly went 5-5 in Day 1 of practice on July 29.

title: NY Giants training camp report, Day 3: Winners, losers, more takeaways
summary: WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — Practice No. 3 of New York Giants training camp is in the books, a two-hour workout on a hot West Virginia afternoon. Winners Darius Alexander — The second-year defensive tackle made a spectacular play to end practice. The Giants were in a last-minute, game on the line situation with the […]
full_text: WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — Practice No. 3 of New York Giants training camp is in the books, a two-hour workout on a hot West Virginia afternoon. Winners Darius Alexander — The second-year defensive tackle made a spectacular play to end practice. The Giants were in a last-minute, game on the line situation with the offense already in field goal range. Quarterback Jaxson Dart tried to get the offense a little closer with a short pass over the middle. Alexander leaped, intercepted the ball, and quickly got down to the ground to seal the “victory”. He and his defensive teammates celebrated wildly. “Probably a presence of mind kind of a play. Probably felt like the ball had to get out,” said head coach John Harbaugh. That’s a heck of a catch. Very athletic play. Game winner. “The thing I probably liked about it the most, now that you mention it, was the fact that he caught it and got down right away. That’s a game winner. He didn’t put the ball at risk and then the defense wins the game. That’s what you kind of want to try to do in that situation.” Some of you might remember Alexander doing this in college: DARIUS ALEXANDER THICC 6!!! pic.twitter.com/EYjGdpgkVd — NFL Draft Files (@NFL_DF) December 26, 2024 Jalin Hyatt — During practice, I did hear Hyatt derisively called “Mr. July.” Considering the past few seasons it is hard to argue that the barb wasn’t appropriate. Hyatt, though, did have three or four catches Friday. The best was a highlight-reel leaping grab between defensive backs Nic Jones and Korie Black on a Jameis Winston throw. Ben Sauls — Friday was Sauls day to kick. He answered the 57-yard game-winning kick made Thursday by undrafted free agent placekicker Dominic Zvada with a 58-yard game winner of his own. Sauls made 6 of 8 kicks on the day, missing one kick that appeared to be from beyond 40 yards and another that was likely from beyond 50. Media was on the opposite end of the field, making judging distances difficult. Arvell Reese — The rookie linebacker made a fantastic play on Friday, using his wingspan to knock away a Dart pass that looked like it was about to be a completion to an open Odell Beckham. Dalen Cambre — If not for Alexander’s interception, the second-year wide receiver/special teamer would have gotten the nod for Play of the Day. Cambre made a fantastic adjustment on a deep ball thrown by Jameis Winston to haul the ball in against tight coverage from rookie cornerback Colton Hood. Losers Jon Runyan — Maybe this should be more about Kayvon Thibodeaux belonging in the “winners” column. Somebody, though, has to lose. Thibodeaux, aligned as a pass rushing defensive tackle, blasted past Runyan to flush Jameis Winston and create a sack for Abdul Carter. Backflips are on hiatus Running back Cam Skattebo, still answering questions about his failed backflip at a recent offseason event, said that backflips are off the table until he scores a touchdown in a game. “We’ll see what game time comes around,” Skattebo said on Friday. “But right now, we’re focused on training camp, and we’ll keep the back flips off the field for now.” Skattebo admitted that he and Harbaugh have had some “rough conversations, being honest with other.” “You can tell he cares, man. You can tell he wants the best for this team,” Skattebo said. “He wants what everybody wants. We all want to win. We all want to win the Super Bowl. We all want to win the championship, everything. So he wants that for us. When guys aren’t doing that, he’s going to make sure that we know that we’re not doing that.” Skattebo acknowledged his impulsivity. “Obviously, I do some dumb things here and there, but I learned from it,” Skattebo said. “My coach talked to me, told me how he felt, and I learned from it. And will I go do that back flip again? Probably not. “So, I mean, we live and we learn and we move on.” Double-edged sword The interception by Alexander was fantastic. The flip side of that great play, though, was that Dart threw a game-ending interception with his team already in position for the field goal it needed. Harbaugh had mixed feeling on the play by Dart. “He’s trying to get yards. I think we’re in field goal range, so he’s got to make that decision probably not to do that,” Harbaugh said. “Maybe he didn’t see the defensive lineman. There’s a lot of nuances to that, but of course, obviously, it’s not a circumstance you want to throw an interception in. We’ll break that down in the meetings tonight and look at the details of it.” The other side of the coin is that it is training camp. “It goes back to what somebody asked me yesterday. You put the quarterback in a tough spot out here. Do you want him pushing the envelope?,” Harbaugh said. “Are you going to criticize him for throwing a pick in training camp? It’s training camp. You’re working through all these things. “You do want him pushing the envelope. You want him competing out there. I think that’s part of what this is all for.” Malik gets a day off After doing individual drills and running routes on air the first two days of training camp, the Giants gave wide receiver Malik Nabers, coming back from a torn ACL, Friday off. “I’d say it’s part of the process. Just got to work through it. And every single day will be what it is,” Harbaugh said. “Every day he’s working real hard. Made a lot of progress, and that’s what we decided to do today.” Other injury notes: Cornerback Art Green worked on the side with trainers, but missed on-field work for a second straight day. Harbaugh said Wednesday that Green is dealing with “a little muscle tightness.” Tight end Tanner Conner left the field late in practice with an unknown injury. title: NY Giants QB Jaxson Dart getting an under center education
summary: WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — It is becoming clearer each day that a heavy portion of the New York Giants’ 2026 offense will be run from under center. On Thursday, starting quarterback Jaxson Dart was under center, unofficially, for 18 of his 30 snaps. That is 60%. On Wednesday, Dart was under center on eight […]
full_text: Jaxson Dart (6) with Darius Slayton during training camp. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — It is becoming clearer each day that a heavy portion of the New York Giants’ 2026 offense will be run from under center. On Thursday, starting quarterback Jaxson Dart was under center, unofficially, for 18 of his 30 snaps. That is 60%. On Wednesday, Dart was under center on eight of 17 snaps I counted (I did miss a few). “It’s part of our offense, what our offense is going to be,” head coach John Harbaugh said on Thursday. “We’re going to be in various elements of it. That’s one of them.” Spending 50% or more of his time under center is a massive change for Dart. It is not something he did much of at Ole Miss. As a rookie with the Giants in 2025, Dart was in the shotgun 87% of the time , under center only 10%, and in the pistol alignment 2%. Aligning the quarterback under center adds variety to the Giants’ options in the run game, and brings real play action into play. Dart said earlier this week that he is “feeling comfortable” under center. “There are a few things mechanically that are different,” Dart said. “Probably just the biggest thing is a little bit of footwork landmarks in the pocket. But we’ve repped the hell out of it, I’m feeling really good with the track that we’re on and I’m feeling comfortable.” Dart has made a handful of nice play-action throws from under center during the first two days of training camp. One that stood out Thursday was a crossing route of roughly 15 yards to tight end Isaiah Likely that was floated nicely over linebacker Tremaine Edmunds. Another was a deep shot down the left sideline to Darnell Mooney. “I don’t know how much he’s done it [under center], but he looks good doing it. It hasn’t been an issue at all,” Harbaugh said. “I would say, under center in the passing game, it does really discipline your footwork because the drops are so important under center. I think it enhances – he would tell you it helps even in the gun, in the pistol, or whatever. It’s just another element.” It is an element we are going to see a lot of in 2026.

Harbaugh said “that might have been talked about” in the course of […]
full_text: Cam Skattebo | Getty Images WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — The Cam Skattebo failed backflip boondoogle is the New York Giants’ story that just won’t die. On Thursday, New York Giants coach John Harbaugh was asked if he had discussed the backflip with the energetic second-year running back. Harbaugh said “that might have been talked about” in the course of five or six recent conversations he has had with Skattebo. Harbaugh had previously reacted to the incident at the Fanatics Fest by jokingly saying “ Dude, at least stick it .” It was clear on Thursday, though, that the veteran head coach really did not see the humor in Skattebo’s flop. “Skatt and I have had, I don’t know, five, six really good conversations since he got back. That might have been talked about in there with some other stuff,” Harbaugh said. “It might have been. It might have been. There might be a good chance. So, I think it’s just part of the ongoing process, just communication, being on the same page, trying to be the best we can be in everything we do. He’s great. He wants to be great. He listens and talks and tells you what he thinks. It’s all good. Skattebo is now practicing fully after last season’s disclocated ankle. Earlier in the week, general manager Joe Schoen said the running back knows the GM would “ rather him not do that .” “The big picture message is you want to take care of yourself. You want to take care of your team. Do everything you can do to be healthy, be back, be right, be good,” Harbaugh said. “What does that mean? It’s not going to be the same situation the next time for anybody. It’s going to be different, so it’s really the principle you talk about.”

title: NY Giants left tackle Andrew Thomas feels the best he has in ‘a long time’
summary: There might have been some small nagging concern regarding New York Giants star left tackle Andrew Thomas as camp opened, considering he was limited in OTAs and minicamp as the coaching staff managed his reps in the spring. Thomas missed the start of the 2025 season as he recovered from a Lisfranc injury, and the […]
full_text: Andrew Thomas | Getty Images There might have been some small nagging concern regarding New York Giants star left tackle Andrew Thomas as camp opened, considering he was limited in OTAs and minicamp as the coaching staff managed his reps in the spring. Thomas missed the start of the 2025 season as he recovered from a Lisfranc injury, and the end of the season when he suffered a hamstring injury. Now, Thomas is almost a “full-go” as camp opens and says that he feels “They were kind of managing my reps today,” Thomas said when asked if he’d get to a full workload at some point in camp. “Like, Bloom (offensive line coach Mike Bloomgren) just tells me when I’m in, when I’m out, and I just try to abide by that but I feel good. This is the best I’ve felt in a long time, so I’m excited for this season.” There are several players on every roster that their team simply does not want to be without. For the Giants, there are very few on that list ahead of Thomas. The Giants obviously want Thomas out there practicing, improving, and building continuity with his linemates. However, they also have to be smart and make sure he’s ready to start the season against the Dallas Cowboys. The venue in West Virginia may help with that as well. Thomas noted that, as a southerner, the weather at Greenbrier is downright chilly. After all, it dipped into the 50’s at night and only got up to a sunny 78 during practice, which is a brand new camp experience for the Georgia product. “It’s amazing,” Thomas said. “I was talking to (offensive lineman) Jon (Runyan Jr.) and I was telling him that I don’t think I’ve ever been a part of a training camp where it’s this cold outside. I’m from the South. Even in Jersey, it gets humid, so I’m not complaining, I’m excited. It’s nice out, just going to continue getting better.” Thomas certainly had a good workout in the second practice, with multiple battles against edge defender Abdul Carter. Carter reportedly had a great practice notching two or three “sacks”, which gives Thomas more to work on and improve for the third practice. “I’ve got to look at the film,” he said. “Just from a feel thing, and just stay more square in my set, trying to stretch the rushers a little bit more. I’ll watch film and see what I can do better.” This is where health and availability really matter. Getting the reps against the Giants’ edge defenders, as well as with his linemates. The Giants haven’t had many opportunities to build continuity along their offensive line in recent years. “Continuity is everything,” Thomas said. “Plus up front, every snap we get, just working through communication and each rep we just get tighter knit and we’ll perform better in the game.” That unit now includes 10th overall pick Sisi Mauigoa, who got the ‘rookie duty’ of running around and firing up the crowd in attendance as well as working as the Giants’ starting right guard. Thomas thought Mauigoa did a good job in both endeavors, both interacting with the fans and in his work on the field. “To be a rookie, like he’s in tune to his assignments,” Thomas said. “He has really good technique. Obviously, he has the physical traits. It’s been exciting to see him put it together so far. “He (Mauigoa) definitely has confidence. Our whole offensive line is just full of personality. He’s done a great job. Like you said, the confidence that he has, you can see it on the field, just the energy he plays with and just going out there attacking, the effort that he plays with to be such a young guy. A lot of times you come out here, you’re thinking a lot when you’re a rookie just trying to understand the speed. But you can see him flying off the ball, he’s excited to get after it.” The Giants’ offensive line was solid — even good — in 2025. It sounds like Thomas thinks there’s even more reason to be excited for 2026.

full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know about after Day 2 of Giants training camp. For Jaxson Dart, it’s time to flip the switch at Giants training camp | The Record WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. − The road from good to greatness for quarterbacks is often not paved with perfection on the practice fields, and especially during the summer. That’s something Jaxson Dart has come to appreciate, but it’s not easy. Aaron Rodgers has always encouraged young quarterbacks to take more risks in practice. New patches for Giants practice jerseys John Harbaugh explains the jersey patches the Giants' players wore in practice today: pic.twitter.com/yVOet3kl3N — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) July 30, 2026 2026 NFL season: How Ward, Dart, Shough, Sanders can improve | ESPN.com Jaxson Dart, New York Giants Where he could get better: Consistency. Dart is an extremely frustrating watch. He has very little consistency to his process as a thrower and a pocket manager. His feet are frequently disconnected from the ground, which affects the timing of his throws and delays his reaction to pressure. His lower-body mechanics change willy-nilly, and he often looks like a kid alone on a basketball court attempting pretend buzzer-beaters, lurching to launch from odd angles for no apparent reason. I’m confident there’s a quality starting QB somewhere in Dart’s game, but it’ll take quite a bit of development to get him there. The good news is that a steady hand is at the mast. With new head coach John Harbaugh comes a legacy of quality Ravens teams. He’ll buy Dart time to grow, as the Giants should improve in all three phases under Harbaugh’s experienced gaze. The offensive brain trust has some worrying names — Matt Nagy, Brian Callahan and Greg Roman — but all three are experienced coaches who should be able to impress upon Dart the importance of a consistent process to create predictable results. Until then, Dart is still more theory than practice. Jaxson Dart has his missing piece of the Giants’ offensive puzzle | New York Post The first practice of the John Harbaugh Era had ended, and there was a bare-chested Jaxson Dart tossing footballs to Malik Nabers. The vision of the young Giants franchise quarterback having the chance to target the electric Go-To Guy he had on the field with him as a rookie for a mere 23 snaps makes Dart’s heart, and Harbaugh’s heart, and the hearts of all Giants fans, sing with joy, and allows all of them to dream, and dream big. Even in limited capacity, Malik Nabers brings ‘aura’ as Giants open training camp | SNY.tv Hope, rejuvenated. It had been 304 days since Nabers tore his ACL and lateral meniscus. Confidence that he would return for the start of the 2026-27 season had waned in the months since. But seeing Nabers there with his quarterback, hours after he took part in individual drills, changed that outlook. There is now justified optimism that the two will share the field against Dallas in 46 days. “There is an aura that he has on the field that is exhilarating,” Dart said. “It’s ‘Leek.’” Veteran DT Johnathan Hankins retires | Pro Football Talk Veteran defensive tackle Johnathan Hankins has hung up his cleats. Hankins, 34, told Jordan Schultz of The Schultz Report that he is retiring after 12 seasons. A second-round pick of the Giants, he also played for the Colts, Raiders and Cowboys. Hankins appeared in 169 career games and was among the league’s premier run-stuffing interior defensive linemen, with 433 tackles, including 44 for loss. title: Jalen Carter contract: Extension details, void years, and “weight bonus”
summary: The Eagles signed Jalen Carter to a four-year extension just as training camp began. We learned that it was a $152 million deal, and now we know some more about how Howie Roseman structured things — and, you guessed it, utilized void years to cushion the cap. According to Spotrac’s breakdown, Carter received $40.8 million […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JULY 30: Jalen Carter #98 of the Philadelphia Eagles reacts during training camp at Jefferson Health Training Complex on July 30, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles signed Jalen Carter to a four-year extension just as training camp began. We learned that it was a $152 million deal, and now we know some more about how Howie Roseman structured things — and, you guessed it, utilized void years to cushion the cap. According to Spotrac’s breakdown, Carter received $40.8 million guaranteed at signing. He also has five option bonuses, and the team added four void years to the deal. As usual, Roseman kept the salary cap in mind — and knowing he’s got some expensive cornerbacks to pay next year — kept the cap hits relatively low for the next few years. DL Jalen Carter's #Eagles Extension ▪️4-yrs, $152M new ▪️$40.8M g'teed at sign ▪️$30M more next March ▪️5 option bonuses ▪️4 void years ▪️$4-yrs, $106.8M practical Cap Hits 2026: $9.1M ($2.1M lost) 2027: $9.5M ($17.6M saved) 2028: $15.5M 2029: $22.2M 2030: $29.4M 2031: $26.2M… — Spotrac (@spotrac) July 31, 2026 ProFootball Talk also reported that the team included $250,000 in bonuses related to a weight check every year. In the report, PFT’s Mike Florio suggested that a “weight bonus” is not typically included in veteran contracts, but throughout the offseason, the coaches mentioned publicly their want for Carter to get in better shape, so it’s not entirely surprising. Good thing for the fourth-year defensive tackle, head coach Nick Sirianni said that Carter returned for training camp in phenomenal shape , so having a set expectation might be a nice guardrail for him and the team. GM Howie Roseman said they had no concerns re-signing Carter , and he hadn’t had any issue off the field since coming to Philly, so his weight might be the only thing they wanted to monitor. All told, the deal looks like yet another win-win for the Eagles organization and for one of the league’s top defensive tackles who deserved a second contract.

summary: When and where: Week 16 at home, Thursday Night Football on Christmas Eve Key additions: RT Braden Smith, S Reed Blakenship, RB David Montgomery Key subtractions: RT Tytus Howard Last season: Had 12 turnovers in the regular season and 8 in two playoff games The question for this team: Is this the last year for […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - JANUARY 18: Head coach DeMeco Ryans of the Houston Texans looks on during the second quarter in the AFC Divisional Playoff game against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on January 18, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images When and where: Week 16 at home, Thursday Night Football on Christmas Eve Key additions: RT Braden Smith, S Reed Blakenship, RB David Montgomery Key subtractions: RT Tytus Howard Last season: Had 12 turnovers in the regular season and 8 in two playoff games The question for this team: Is this the last year for CJ Stroud? Only two active coaches have won a playoff game in each of the last three seasons: Sean McVay and DeMeco Ryans. Ryans has done so with a rookie QB, a QB who played like a rookie, and a QB whose play has the team seeing and waiting on a contract extension. All three QBs are the same person, CJ Stroud. Who, if you missed it, cut his hair. He looks like a guy with a regular job. In 2025 only the Seahawks gave up fewer points than the Texans, and barely so, 3 points. But defenses can be fickle. Last year they were 14th, in 2023 they were 11th. This should once again be a top defense, the foundations are there. Will Anderson is excellent, and Danielle Hunter has had 10.5+ sacks in each of the six full seasons he has played in the last eight years. Derek Stingley and Kamari Lassiter are an excellent CB duo. The rest of the defense is filled with a good mix of guys on their rookie deals and established veterans. They beat up some bad teams in 2025, but also held the Rams, Bills, 49ers, and early season Bucs to less than 21 points. But they went 2-2 in those games because the offense can’t get its act together. CJ Stroud threw 4 TDs in a 44-10 demolishing of the Cooper Rush-led Ravens, then in the next game, which followed their bye, the Texans scored 19 points against the Seahawks, with Stroud completing 47% of his passes. They dropped 36 on the Jaguars but 31 combined in the game before and after. In games against the Chiefs, Patriots, and Seahawks the defense had 10 takeaways, but the Texans scored fewer than 20 points in all three and went 1-2. Next year is the last year of Stroud’s contract. This year very well could be his last with the Texans.

title: Eagles’ reborn running game can take pressure off Jalen Hurts
summary: As training camp opens this week, there is no player on the Eagles under the microscope more than Jalen Hurts. The entire fanbase is intently studying Sean Mannion’s new offense and how their Super Bowl winning quarterback will evolve in it. Through Wednesday and Thursday’s first two practices, it appears the offense will look very […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JULY 30: Saquon Barkley #26 of the Philadelphia Eagles smiles during training camp at Jefferson Health Training Complex on July 30, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images As training camp opens this week, there is no player on the Eagles under the microscope more than Jalen Hurts. The entire fanbase is intently studying Sean Mannion’s new offense and how their Super Bowl winning quarterback will evolve in it. Through Wednesday and Thursday’s first two practices, it appears the offense will look very different from the ones Hurts has played in through his first five seasons. While it remains to be seen how Hurts will fare in the passing game and what it will mean for him as a runner, it seems clear the new offense should be a boon for the running game and, in particular, Saquon Barkley and Tank Bigsby. By the end of last season, the Eagles’ offensive line was an injury-plagued and ineffective group playing in an offense that was too predictable and asked for the linemen to do too much. It resulted in a massive drop in production from the run game and Barkley in particular. The Birds had the second-most rushing yards in 2024 (3,048) and averaged 4.9 yards per carry. Last year, they were 18th in rushing yards (1.988) and averaged just 4.2 yards per carry. While Barkley did total 1,140 yards on the ground, it obviously paled in comparison to his legendary 2,005 yard season the year before. It’s actually kind of a miracle he was able to pile up as many yards as he did. Barkley’s backfield mate, Tank Bigsby, was acquired at the start of last season and didn’t begin to play regularly until Week 8 against the Giants, when he burst onto the scene with a nine-carry, 104-yard performance. He only had 356 yards rushing but did so on just 63 carries, averaging 5.7 yards per attempt. The early reports on the running backs, Bigsby in particular, are encouraging. Very early into practice and Eagles RB Tank Bigsby has already made some nice plays. Good run up the middle and then a catch-and-run from the flag to shake a defender for YAC. — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) July 29, 2026 We all know what Barkley can do, and much of last year’s struggles were due to an offensive line that saw an injured Cam Jurgens getting beat up and manhandled on a weekly basis as he fought through a lot of pain. Same for guard Landon Dickerson, who was nowhere near the same player he had been throughout his career. And Lane Johnson missed the team’s final eight games with a foot injury that was originally only supposed to keep him out 2-3 weeks. The line just never got healthy or productive. So it’s exciting to hear that Johnson and Jordan Mailata are so excited about what they saw during the spring practices. Lane Johnson says the Eagles’ new scheme is OL friendly because it makes the offense less predictable and he has more blocking help. — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) July 29, 2026 Eagles LT Jordan Mailata seems just as excited as Lane Johnson about the scheme changes: “It is fun seeing now, understanding the concept of stressing the defense. You kinda ask yourself ‘offensive linemen have done this in the league for years?’ This is fun!” pic.twitter.com/S3sNsaDqGo — Anthony DiBona (@DiBonaNFL) July 30, 2026 Former offensive coordinator Kevin Patullo’s vanilla and obvious gameplans allowed defenses to key in on Barkley, too. It was a recipe for disaster. Imagine having a playbook in which plays are designed to make it unclear to the defense whether the upcoming play was going to be a run or a pass, a playbook where both aspects of the offense worked off one another. Seems impossible, but it can happen! Things should be different in 2026. And that would be the very best thing to take the pressure off Hurts and the revamped passing attack. There is enough talent on this offense that it is conceivable Barkley and Bigsby could each go over 1,000 yards. In fact, let me go ahead and make that prediction. Saquon Barkley and Tank Bigsby will both clear 1,000 yards rushing this season. If that happens, and if Mannion’s offense resembles anything like what we’ve seen from San Francisco, Los Angeles or Green Bay, the ground game will once again return to being one of the best in the league. Welcome news for Jalen Hurts, to be sure.

summary: Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … George Pickens, CeeDee Lamb turn in big day at Dallas Cowboys training camp – Star-TelegramIn early July, Prescott took the offensive skill players on an annual trip to bond and workout together for three days. full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - NOVEMBER 23: Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott (4) gets hit by Philadelphia Eagles linebacker Zack Baun (53) during the game between the Dallas Cowboys and the Philadelphia Eagles on November 23, 2025 at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Matthew Pearce/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … George Pickens, CeeDee Lamb turn in big day at Dallas Cowboys training camp – Star-Telegram In early July, Prescott took the offensive skill players on an annual trip to bond and workout together for three days. This year, the destination was Park City, Utah where they spent some time on the lake in cool weather. While they were on the trip, Prescott presented a nickname for the offense heading into 2026 that he said was met with a lot of positive reviews: GOTI, meaning “Greatest Offense There Is”. “We were close to some historic things last year,” Prescott said. “And when you have the guys [on the offense], why can’t we be? Let’s be the Greatest Offense There Is. You’ve heard of the Greatest Show On Turf and all of the other nicknames. We take pride in it, and it’s the way we’ve been practicing.” Eagles Training Camp Practice Notes: Tank Bigsby must be more involved in the offense this year! – BGN Tank Bigsby broke off multiple long runs to the end zone. He’s not someone you need to lock in on in order to notice him at practice; the way he moves is really eye-catching. I know I’ve been beating this drum a lot but I just can’t stop thinking about how the Eagles MUST get him more involved this season. He’s simply too electric to be an afterthought in this offense. Bigsby logged just 3.6 carries per game last season … and that’s with him benefiting from garbage time/the Eagles resting their starters in Week 18. His workload needs to be bigger in 2026. Eagles Training Camp Observations, Day 2: Defense Dominates – Go Birds! Podcast Eliot Shorr-Parks and Brandon Lee Gowton recap the second day of Eagles Training Camp and discuss their expectations for the Birds’ offense after another day of the getting dominated by the defense. 2026 NFL fantasy football: 10 overvalued, undervalued NFL players to know before you draft – NFL.com OVERVALUED — From a passing perspective, Jalen Hurts had a decent 2025, tossing a career-high 25 touchdowns and topping 3,000 yards for the fourth time in five seasons as the starter. However, he dropped to just 421 yards and eight touchdowns rushing, both fewest since taking the helm in 2021. Specifically, with Jason Kelce gone and the tush push somewhat neutered, Hurts scored just five TDs from inside the 3-yard line last season, fewest as the starter and six fewer than he had in both 2023 and 2024 (11). As a result, he finished as the QB8 in fantasy, well below the elite tier he’d previously called home. With A.J. Brown’s departure and a(nother) first-time offensive coordinator in Sean Mannion, it’s tough to see Hurts’ passing numbers really improving. And with the Eagles lacking their former dominance at the goal line, the QB5 price tag in the fifth round is simply too high. Seven takeaways from Vic Fangio’s initial training camp press conference – PhillyVoice Temper expectations for Uar Bernard Fangio was asked what the plan is for Bernard. “The ‘PP Plan,’ lots of patience and lots of persistence. The day he put on a helmet here was the first time he ever put on a helmet. He hasn’t had shoulder pads on yet. That would be a new experience for him. Everybody, including himself and us, needs to temper any expectations down. He’s got a process to go through. Process, that’s a bad word around here [jokingly].” #JimmySays: I watched a little bit of Bernard with the developmental players during the Eagles’ first day of practice, and, uh, he’s got a long, loooong way to go. Training Camp – Day 2 – Iggles Blitz The defense took center stage on Day 2 of Training Camp. That’s no surprise since the Eagles should be a Top 5 defense in the league this season. The unit has playmakers at all three levels and is very talented overall. Eagles 53-man roster projection: How many WRs will Howie Roseman keep? – The Athletic Offensive line. Kubena (9): Lane Johnson, Jordan Mailata, Markel Bell, Fred Johnson, Cam Jurgens, Landon Dickerson, Tyler Steen, Myles Hinton, Drew Kendall. The swing tackle battle is still in … full swing between Bell and Fred Johnson. But given Philadelphia’s third-round investment in Bell, the odds are stacked against Fred Johnson. Hinton, a sixth-round pick in 2025, continues to see reps at second-team left guard. Kendall is getting second-team reps at guard, too. I have not seen Kendall take snaps at center yet in training camp, but the Eagles know from his days at Boston College he can play the position. Berman (10): Jordan Mailata, Landon Dickerson, Cam Jurgens, Tyler Steen, Lane Johnson, Fred Johnson, Markel Bell, Drew Kendall, Myles Hinton, Micah Morris. I have the Eagles going deeper on the offensive line to develop their young linemen. Morris, a sixth-round pick who plays on the interior, makes sense to keep. Cameron Williams left practice early Thursday; it’ll be interesting to monitor his status. I was debating between Williams and Hinton before the injury and leaned toward Hinton because of position flexibility. Perhaps the Eagles will keep Michael Jordan because of his starting experience. What about Willie Lampkin, a player who intrigued the front office when it claimed him off waivers last summer? Eagles practice observations: Tank Bigsby and run game juice; expendable cornerbacks; Jake Elliott’s pressure – Inquirer Kicking and redeeming. I’m going to start with how practice started: Jake Elliott kicking field goals. It might not be as sexy as the new offense or how the rookies look, but the Eagles need Elliott to return to form this season. He’s coming off back-to-back down years, and yet the team didn’t add competition in camp. Kickers are essentially competing with whoever is on the street. But special teams coordinator Michael Clay’s comment about Elliott during the spring — that his job was to help the 10-year veteran “fall in love with the game again” — made me wonder if Elliott could have benefited from additional pressure. His camp got off to a solid start in windy conditions. He made 6 of 7 kicks, hitting from around 33, 35, 37, 43, 43 and 46 yards. He hooked a 40-yard try wide left. Elliott has a natural tendency to draw the ball, and the wind was blowing in that direction, so it was a tough kick from the right hash mark. Nevertheless, he has more riding on this summer’s performance than he has in years. Inside the Jalen Carter deal – PFT Earlier this week, Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter became the highest-paid interior defensive lineman in NFL history. The full details are now out. Here’s the breakdown, per a source with knowledge of the terms. The best news of Eagles camp: A healthy Landon Dickerson and Cam Jurgens – NBCSP Considering what Cam Jurgens and Landon Dickerson have been through the last couple years and the questions they faced coming into training camp, that’s awfully encouraging. Both dealt with serious injuries during the 2024 Super Bowl run, and last year Jurgens missed three games with a knee injury and dealt with lingering back pain, and although he did make his second straight Pro Bowl he was just a shell of his usual self. And this time last year Dickerson was out with a torn meniscus that had to be scoped and then dealt with back and ankle injuries during the season. Although he played 16 of 18 games, he was also just a shell of his three-time Pro Bowl self. Both spent time this offseason in Medellin, Columbia, receiving stem-cell treatments to try to get healthy enough to regain their elite form, and here we are at training camp and both are full-go and look fine. It’s only a couple days, but it’s awfully encouraging seeing both of them out there running around with no…

Needless to say, it puts Alex Highsmith in a difficult position. With two years […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - JANUARY 4: Alex Highsmith #56 of the Pittsburgh Steelers looks on looks on during the national anthem prior to an NFL football game against the Baltimore Ravens at Acrisure Stadium on January 04, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The future may be complicated for one Pro Bowl Pittsburgh Steelers edge rusher. T.J. Watt signed a new deal to pay $41 million per year before week one last year, and Nick Herbig inked a four-year, $100 million contract this offseason. Needless to say, it puts Alex Highsmith in a difficult position. With two years remaining on his contract, Highsmith remains a valuable part of the highest-paid defense in football. His future could also be in doubt after the Steelers committed more money to two players at the same position over the last two offseasons. Regardless, Highsmith said after practice on Friday that he wants to remain with the Steelers his entire career. “That’s my dream,” Highsmith said. “I do want to be a Steeler for life.” Highsmith will turn 30 next week and is entering his seventh season in Pittsburgh. In 90 games, Highsmith owns 45 sacks, 337 tackles, 10 forced fumbles, 10 passes defended, and three interceptions. Despite the uncertainty, Highsmith is focused on this season and getting the Steelers back over the hump. “I just want to go out there and do whatever I can to help bring another Super Bowl to this team and city,” Highsmith said. “I do want to be a Steeler for life, so for me, I’m just excited for this year.” The outside linebackers are the deepest and most talented group on the roster. “Our group, we’re the best group in the league edge-wise. The three of us and Jack (Sawyer),” Highsmith said. “I think we’re going to do some special things.” Let us know what you think in the comments . summary: LATROBE – Day Three of Pittsburgh Steelers training camp was unlike any Steelers practice I’ve covered in terms of its layout. full_text: Jul 29, 2026; Latrobe, PA, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy talks with quarterback Will Howard (18) during a practice session at Saint Vincent College. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect LATROBE – Day Three of Pittsburgh Steelers training camp was unlike any Steelers practice I’ve covered in terms of its layout. It was an incredibly light day for the Steelers that featured players in caps and bucket hats rather than helmets as the team ran a walkthrough for the entire two hour practice. The plays were ran at 50-60 percent speed, and it was a very energetic, laid back environment. So, with that as a prerequisite, there frankly wasn’t much to take away from Day Three, but Joey Bray and I will both share the few takeaways we had from Friday morning’s practice. Germie Bernard, Roman Wilson movement on offense Germie Bernard took the field with the First-Team during practice, working largely from the slot while DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman were on the outside. Roman Wilson took some reps on the outside with the second team. This was by design, as head coach Mike McCarthy said ahead of practice that he would be looking to give Wilson some outside reps as to not pigeon hole him at one spot. – Jarrett Bailey Get used to seeing Aaron Rodgers under center more Throughout practice, Aaron Rodgers was under center a lot. This is something that Rodgers had stressed in his pre-training camp presser on Tuesday. He wants to be under center more this season and it looks like McCarthy is going to grant his wish and give him those opportunities this season. – Joey Bray Mike McCarthy watched Will Howard and Drew Allar closely Mike McCarthy spent the majority of practice with the third and fourth teams coaching up Will Howard and Drew Allar. Howard is the guy McCarthy has arguably talked up the most this offseason, while Allar is the hand picked developmental quarterback. It’s refreshing to see a head coach so involved with the development of his young quarterbacks. If anything, it shows that McCarthy is looking toward the future and wants to get every opportunity he can at these young guys. It would be much better for the Steelers long term if one of the guys on the roster ends up being their future franchise guy, and McCarthy knows that. Howard has much more to prove over the next few weeks of camp and preseason compared to Allar, but getting that increased one-on-one time with their new head coach is crucial. – Joey Bray Mike McCarthy’s impact is already being seen These first handful of practices have gone a long way to let everyone know this is Mike McCarthy’s team now. Practices are meticulous, yet efficient. And today, even in a more laid back setting, the energy was brought by every player. We never saw a practice like this under Mike Tomlin. They could often feel too repetitive, which led to sluggish days that lacked drive. Offense has become a much larger focus. Seven-on-sevens, half-field drills, 6-on-8 offense-defense, and full team drills and scrimmage have all taken place over the first three days, and there have been plenty of reps to go around, allowing just about every player to get a taste of offense vs. defense in some way. These are much different than the days in Latrobe that we grew accustomed to seeing over the last two decades, which is something important to establish early on for a new head coach – McCarthy’s done that, and then some. – Jarrett Bailey Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Mike McCarthy sees big things coming for Asante Samuel Jr
summary: Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy made it clear that he believes cornerback Asante Samuel Jr. can become an important part of the team’s defense, offering one of his strongest endorsements yet for the talented defensive back. Speaking about Samuel’s outlook, McCarthy expressed confidence in both the player’s ability and his fit within Pittsburgh’s defensive […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - JANUARY 12: Brandin Echols #26 of the Pittsburgh Steelers and Asante Samuel Jr. #22 of the Pittsburgh Steelers celebrate after an interception in the third quarter of an NFL wild card playoff game against the Houston Texans at Acrisure Stadium on January 12, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy made it clear that he believes cornerback Asante Samuel Jr. can become an important part of the team’s defense, offering one of his strongest endorsements yet for the talented defensive back. Speaking about Samuel’s outlook, McCarthy expressed confidence in both the player’s ability and his fit within Pittsburgh’s defensive plans. “I know personally, I’m counting on him,” McCarthy said . “He’s frankly been one of my favorite players since I’ve arrived here.” Those comments suggest McCarthy envisions a meaningful role for Samuel rather than simply adding depth to the secondary. After entering training camp with questions surrounding the cornerback rotation, Samuel appears to have earned the trust of the Steelers’ coaching staff through his work and versatility. The former second-round pick has been putting his talent on display through the first week of training camp, totaling three pass breakups during team drills while playing a starting role alongside Jamel Dean with both Joey Porter and Jalen Ramsey not practicing. With McCarthy publicly stating that he’s counting on Samuel, expectations are growing that the veteran defensive back will play a significant role when the Steelers open the regular season. title: 49ers LT Trent Williams is ‘trying to soak in every day’ in his final couple of years in the NFL
summary: Not many players make it to ten years in the NFL and are still considered among the best at their positions. For Trent Williams, he’s entering Year 16 while being widely considered a top-5 left tackle. Williams spoke to the media earlier this week about whether his approach is changing heading into training camp as […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - JUNE 03: Trent Williams #71 of the San Francisco 49ers speaks with the media after a team OTA practice at SAP Performance Facility on June 3, 2026 in Santa Clara, CA. (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Not many players make it to ten years in the NFL and are still considered among the best at their positions. For Trent Williams, he’s entering Year 16 while being widely considered a top-5 left tackle. Williams spoke to the media earlier this week about whether his approach is changing heading into training camp as he heads into the final couple of seasons in his career. Williams said: “I wouldn’t say it changed my urgency, but it does change my mind frame a little bit. Like, instead of just coming to work, I actually try to soak it in. I just don’t know. Obviously, it could be my last two years. It’s probably the plan. So I’m just really trying to soak in every day, build these relationships, take advantage of it, because once that window closes, it generally don’t open back up.” As for Williams’ preparation heading into the year, he said this offseason he focused more on “remaining explosive” and speed training, so that he can “remain nimble at the spry age of 38.” One talking point since Kyle Shanahan’s accident has been how the locker room would react. Williams seems unbothered in that regard: “Nah, we gotta lot of vets, man. He really can be on autopilot. We got that locker room.” One of the big changes for Williams is a new-look defense. The Niners have changed defensive coordinators, but the scheme has been the same since Williams has been on the roster: Everything is different. We’ve been going against the same defense, in a team environment, since I’ve been here. It’s always been a four-down front. It’s all different. Obviously, we’re not brand new to it. We played it a lot when Rah[eem Morris] was in L.A. We played it last year in Atlanta. It’s actually one of those defenses that a lot of people try to throw in their repertoire. So getting work on it early in camp and being able to do it as much as we have is going to help us in the season. Williams was describing a 5-man front, or as he said, “the presentation of a 5-man front.” From there, you can play all sorts of games, like dropping defenders or messing with the protection of the offensive line. It won’t be long until Williams is going 1-on-1 with Nick Bosa. Trent said he couldn’t tell that Bosa ever suffered an injury. That’s how good he looks: “Most people, when they have a knee injury that’s that catastrophic. You can see something. You can see it in the atrophy. In the muscle and the legs. You can see something. I mean, Bosa looks better than he did before he got hurt last year.” One player Williams could be playing next to is second-year pro Connor Colby. Williams said he’s “excited” to see Colby this year. Here’s more from Trent about Colby: Just confidence. As an 0-lineman, you can see confidence not in just the personality, it’s more in the movements. You can see his pass sets, and how he’s coming along. He’s just sure of himself. Last year, you could tell there’s, we throw a lot at him. A lot of the things we know today, it took us five, six years to learn. Any time you get a guy coming in first year, as much as we want him to be the best he can be, realistically, that information is just too much for any one person in one year. I can tell now that he is very confident in which direction he’s going. He knows his plays. So now it’s allowing him to be the player he knows he can be once the ball is snapped. Life should be a little easier for Colby in Year 2 playing next to Williams, given how great his communication and overall skill are.
